items.title: UNICEF urges Kenya to protect children’s budgets amid foreign aid cuts
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 23 – The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has urged national and county governments to protect funding for education, healthcare, child protection and social protection amid declining international aid, warning that funding cuts could expose vulnerable children to greater
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 23 – The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has urged national and county governments to protect funding for education, healthcare, child protection and social protection amid declining international aid, warning that funding cuts could expose vulnerable children to greater risks.
UNICEF Representative to Kenya Dr Shaheen Nilofer made the appeal during World Children’s Day celebrations held at the United Nations Office at Nairobi on Friday, November 20, urging governments to prioritise children in budget allocations.
“Investing in children is no rocket science. You can still be able to redeploy and re-prioritise,” Nilofer said, responding to concerns about declining official development assistance and its impact on services for children.
She warned that reduced funding could disproportionately affect children facing poverty, disability and limited access to essential services, increasing their vulnerability to exploitation and hazardous work.
Nilofer called on governments to protect budgets supporting education, healthcare, child protection and social assistance programmes, including grants for orphans and vulnerable children.
She said governments must balance infrastructure investments with spending on services that directly benefit children, particularly those from disadvantaged households.
The UNICEF representative also urged county assemblies to prioritise children when approving budgets, noting that decisions at both national and county levels determine whether essential services reach those who need them.
“We’re reminding that members of the county assembly, when you’re doing a budgeting, please make sure the centrality of the children must be in front of the budget,” she said.
Nilofer cited children in counties such as Mandera and Turkana, noting that poverty, disability and other disadvantages can overlap, limiting access to education, healthcare and protection services.
She also warned that inadequate social support could expose some children to hazardous employment, including unregulated mining activities in parts of Migori and Turkana.
On declining international funding, Nilofer said UNICEF was working with governments and development partners to identify ways of sustaining essential services.
She noted that the private sector also had a responsibility to support programmes benefiting children, while governments needed to strengthen domestic resource mobilisation to reduce reliance on foreign assistance.
Despite the challenges, Nilofer acknowledged progress made by Kenya in education, healthcare and efforts to address harmful practices affecting children.
She said improvements in school enrolment, maternal and child health and other social programmes reflected contributions from government institutions, development partners and civil society organisations.
However, she noted that recurring emergencies, including droughts, floods and disease outbreaks, continued to undermine progress and place additional pressure on services targeting vulnerable communities.
The concerns come amid persistent inequalities in access to basic services among children in Kenya, particularly in rural communities, where poverty and limited access to healthcare, education and adequate housing continue to affect their welfare.
Earlier this month, Kenya became the 80th country to sign the Intergovernmental Declaration on Children, Youth and Climate Action, committing to place children’s rights and needs at the centre of climate policies and investments.
The declaration came amid concerns that approximately 12 million of Kenya’s 24.6 million children face moderate to very high risks from climate change and disasters.
Friday’s World Children’s Day celebrations were held under the theme “My Day, My Rights, My Future,” with UNICEF bringing together children and their caregivers for activities aimed at raising awareness of children’s rights.
The event featured a treasure hunt, games and other interactive activities through which children learned about their rights while engaging with their peers.
Among the participants was 12-year-old Raziel, who said the treasure hunt was his favourite activity and that the celebration had helped him better understand children’s rights.
“I learned that children deserve a lot of rights like an adult,” Raziel said.
He encouraged people to treat children with kindness, noting that they would play an important role in shaping the future.
Parents attending the celebrations similarly called for greater awareness of children’s rights and the responsibilities of families and communities in protecting them.
Nyagwaga Luoch Koriom, who attended the event with her two children aged 10 and 13, said the celebration provided an opportunity for parents and guardians to reflect on how they treat children.
She emphasised the importance of education, basic needs and protection from abuse, urging communities to act when they witness mistreatment.
“For example, right to clothing, right to school, and every other right that we know,” she said, explaining the rights parents and guardians should uphold.
Koriom also called for greater attention to girls’ education and the protection of children from sexual abuse and other forms of violence.
The celebrations formed part of activities marking World Children’s Day, observed annually on November 20 to commemorate the adoption of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989.
The convention recognises children’s rights to survival, development, protection and participation in decisions affecting their lives.
The messages from UNICEF, parents and children highlighted the need to match commitments to children’s rights with practical measures, including sustained funding for essential services and stronger protection for vulnerable children.

items.title: Purdy carves up Vikings defence as 49ers seal win in Mexico
items.summary:
San Francisco 49ers 35-10 Minnesota Vikings: Brock Purdy dismantles Vikings defence with three touchdown passes
Brock Purdy starred as San Francisco 49ers extended their season record to 9-1 with a 35-10 win against Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City; Purdy threw three touchdown passes and gained 255
items.text:
San Francisco 49ers 35-10 Minnesota Vikings: Brock Purdy dismantles Vikings defence with three touchdown passes
Brock Purdy starred as San Francisco 49ers extended their season record to 9-1 with a 35-10 win against Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City; Purdy threw three touchdown passes and gained 255 yards; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports
Monday 23 November 2026 07:43, UK
Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers offence turned what was billed as a heavyweight clash between two of the NFL’s top units into a one-sided contest, as Kyle Shanahan’s side delivered a commanding 35–10 victory in Mexico City.
Played in front of a raucous, pro-49ers crowd at Estadio Azteca, the game had been billed as a heavyweight showdown between one of the NFL's most dangerous offences, San Francisco (9ǃ), and a Minnesota Vikings (7ǅ) defence that had unsettled quarterbacks throughout the season with its aggressive blitz-heavy approach.
However, Purdy proved more than equal to the challenge, delivering an imperious performance and carving up the Minnesota defence with three touchdown passes in the first half alone.
"You have to be aggressive and don't second-guess yourself," Purdy said.
"Obviously, try to read it the best you can, but when you have players that can go get the ball, allow them to go and make plays.
"I feel like our guys did that around me today. It wasn't a one-man show. It was a really good team effort."
'Purdy was so quick'
Coordinator Brian Flores' schemes didn't work at all against the 49ers quarterback, who orchestrated three touchdown drives on the Niners' first four possessions.
"He was so good. He was quick, he was confident, he threw strikes," said tight end George Kittle, who caught two TD passes.
"He's playing with confidence, he understands the offense, he is confident in the offense. He knows the offense. When he goes out there he has this aura in the huddle."
49ers set the tone early
San Francisco headed into half-time with a commanding 28-10 lead, fuelled by Purdy's outstanding performance and a pick-six from Ji'Ayir Brown, who intercepted Kirk Cousins and returned it for a touchdown.
The 49ers set the tone from the outset, marching downfield on an impressive seven-play, 72-yard opening drive. Purdy completed all four of his passes for 55 yards, capping the possession with a 17-yard touchdown pass to George Kittle.
After being forced to punt on their second possession, San Francisco quickly regained momentum, with Purdy orchestrating touchdown drives on each of their next two possessions.
He threw an eight-yard touchdown pass to Kittle to make it 14ǉ before connecting with Mike Evans for a four-yard score to extend the lead to 21.
Brown then intercepted Cousins on the Vikings' next play from scrimmage and returned it 18 yards for a touchdown, further extending San Francisco's advantage.
The 49ers continued to impress after the break, producing a superb 98-yard touchdown drive that featured chants of "MVP!" for Purdy. The possession was capped off by Christian McCaffrey's six-yard touchdown run, effectively putting the game beyond doubt early in the fourth quarter.
Purdy finished 21 of 26 for 255 yards and a remarkable passer rating of 146, more than double the league-low 69.5 rating Minnesota's defence had allowed opponents entering the game.
Reflecting on his quarterback's performance, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said: "Seemed like he played a lot better than a lot of other guys have versus them, because not many people play that good versus that defence.
"There's a reason for that. It's a huge challenge. It was hard looking at it all week. Brock didn't get rattled, which he really never does. I think it says a lot about Brock."
However, the emphatic victory was overshadowed by a serious injury to right tackle Colton McKivitz, who broke and dislocated his left ankle during the second quarter.
McKivitz was injured at the end of a four-yard run by McCaffrey, after being caught in a collision with opposing players. The severity of the injury was immediately apparent, with team-mates visibly distressed as medical staff rushed onto the field. Left tackle Trent Williams slammed his helmet to the ground, while several 49ers players took a knee as McKivitz received treatment.
Head coach Shanahan later confirmed that the injury was similar to the one that brought linebacker Fred Warner's season to an end last October.
"That was really crushing," Shanahan said. "Colton has had an unbelievable year. It was tough to see him go down like that."
Despite the convincing victory, McKivitz's injury provided a sobering moment for San Francisco, with the team now facing the prospect of being without a key member of its offensive line.
Cousins gains unwanted NFL record
It's the Vikings' second defeat in three weeks, with Cousins also throwing a pick-six in Week Nine for the Las Vegas Raiders, before he was traded back to Minnesota.
He became the first player ever to throw a pick-six for two teams against the same opponent in a season.
Cousins went 26 for 38 for 235 yards and was unable to follow up his winning performance last week at Green Bay.
"There's no group that I have more confidence in than not only those players on defense and that coaching staff." Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said.
"There's just no really other way to put it. We just got beat tonight.
"They made some plays. I think the quarterback [Purdy] is really good and they got a bunch of really good players and they execute at a really high level."
The 49ers will look to extend their 9-1 record as they welcome Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, while the Vikings face off against the Atlanta Falcons in Minneapolis on the same night.

items.text:
One of football's most-hyped 16-year-olds - what next for JJ Gabriel?
- Published
It has been one of the biggest transfer sagas of the year - around a player who has never played competitive football.
Forward JJ Gabriel, who has recently turned 16, walked out on Manchester United in September and now has a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid.
Before even playing a senior game - barring friendlies - he has told Spanish newspaper Marca his "dream is to win the Ballon d'Or".
Gabriel's real name is Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill - with Cypriot and Irish lineage - but he changed his name, reportedly for commercial purposes.
His father, London-born Joe O'Cearuill, played twice for the Republic of Ireland - but the highest level he played at club level was a loan spell with Brighton in League One and one minute in the Uefa Cup with St Patrick's Athletic. He has been actively involved in his son's career.
Gabriel was scheduled to become Manchester United's youngest ever player in the Carabao Cup against Brighton on 16 September, but had told the club he planned to leave by then.
How long will Gabriel have to wait for a first-team debut now? In the past 10 years Real have only handed two debuts to 17-year-olds and none to a 16-year-old.
When Real boss Jose Mourinho was asked about Gabriel on Friday, he said: "I don't have a feeling [about Gabriel]. I don't have a feeling with players who don't work with me."
In fact, Real have not even announced anything yet - despite Gabriel posting a 50-second video montage on social media saying goodbye to United this week.
- Madrid-bound Gabriel posts farewell Man Utd message 
  - Published5 days ago
- Why schoolboys have become a huge part of football's transfer market 
  - Published25 September
Why did Real Madrid want Gabriel?
For a while now Madrid have been getting the best young talents early and turning them into Galacticos before they cost in excess of 100m euros.
Vinicius Junior and Rodrygo came that way, then Endrick - and Gabriel is seen as the next.
It fits the policy run by Jose Angel Sanchez, the director general, and Juni Calafat, head of scouting. It is a long-term bet on one of the most promising young players in the international game.
Barcelona looked at him too, and backed away because the commissions were too high. Madrid believe in the player so much that they were willing to pay whatever it took to get the deal done.
The expectations are very high and the aim is for him to reach the first team. They want him at Castilla - Real's reserve team - but the situation right now does not allow it.
Castilla and Real Madrid C cannot sign players until January, so for the time being he is expected to play for the Juvenil - the under-18s.
Madrid also learned from the Martin Odegaard period that training with the first team while playing for the B side is a bad idea. So the plan is a spell in the B side, and when he is ready, Gabriel jumps straight into the first team.
Where Madrid are less happy is with how things have unfolded. Madrid wanted to set the timing themselves and be discreet, because they do not want problems with Manchester United and do not want to upset anyone. At Real Madrid, nobody is bigger than the club.
The idea was to keep everything quiet until January and announce it then. But with Gabriel already training in Madrid, the secret was never going to last.
The super-agent behind the move
Who is Gabriel's new agent, Ali Barat?
"Players are moving to him because his reputation is that he'll get you a move to a bigger club," one Premier League club source told BBC Sport.
Dubai-based Barat does not just consider himself a super-agent, but a "boutique" super-agent.
Born in Iran and raised in London, Barat says he fell into football almost by accident after many years in international business.
After initially working as an intermediary at low-level clubs, he founded Epic Sports in January 2020.
His major football experience before that? The football game Championship Manager.
"I was always trading players," he told ESPN this year. "I was obsessed with every single player around the world."
This was not just about living out a fantasy in the real world. Barat was drawn into the profession because of the vast sums agents can earn in commission.
What makes his agency "boutique"? Unlike the top operations which have a huge number of players on their books, Epic Sports aims to have just 22 - two for each position.
This, Barat argues, ensures there is never any conflict of interest in how he represents his players.
Barat offers bespoke management of a player's career and came to prominence in the summer of 2025 when 15 of his players moved on.
This included Dean Huijsen joining Real Madrid, Nicolas Jackson moving to Bayern Munich and Xavi Simons signing for Tottenham Hotspur. Noni Madueke left Chelsea for Arsenal, and the Gunners signed Piero Hincapie.
This led to Barat being named Golden Boy Best Agent for the second time in three years.
Yet he is largely the figurehead, with agents working on his behalf around Europe. For instance, Epic has three other agents registered with the English Football Association (FA).
Barat, who also brokered Moises Caicedo's move to Chelsea, says he uses social media, and in particular influencer Fabrizio Romano, to amplify stories and agree transfers on his terms.
He is an unashamed self-publicist, too.
"Ali Barat redefines the game again," read an Epic Sports press release to announce Jackson's loan move to Bayern. No other agency seems to promote itself in this way.
The largely AI-generated video which announced Gabriel had joined Epic Sports was right on brand.
Gabriel's deal is part of a new venture: Epic Future - and this presents an ethical problem.
"It is about targeting the biggest young players, especially where they're not necessarily on the longest contracts," a Premier League source said. "And move them overseas for cheap fees.

items.summary:
Alcaraz storms past world number one Zverev to win maiden ATP Finals title
Alcaraz joins an exclusive list, becoming one of only four men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals.
Seven-time Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz powered past world number one Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 (9-7) on Sun
items.text:
Alcaraz storms past world number one Zverev to win maiden ATP Finals title
Alcaraz joins an exclusive list, becoming one of only four men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals.
Seven-time Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz powered past world number one Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 (9-7) on Sunday to win his maiden ATP Finals title.
The Spaniard, who returned at the US Open after a four-month break due to a wrist injury, saved three set points in the tiebreak before completing his 14th consecutive victory and ending the year with a third straight title, having also triumphed in Vienna and Paris.
The 23-year-old, who is the youngest man to have completed the career Grand Slam, secured the biggest tour title that had eluded him after finishing runner-up at the ATP Finals last year.
Since losing in the quarterfinals of the 2026 US Open, he has won four titles with a 22-1 record.
“For me, it’s been an amazing week,” Alcaraz said. “I couldn’t have ended the week in a better way. I’m just really proud and really happy with everything I have done this week.
“I’ve been through really difficult moments within myself, with my team, and we went through everything playing great tennis. This trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time.
“It means the world to me.”
For Zverev, the defeat brought an end to his most successful season, in which he won his first two Grand Slam titles and rose to the top of the world rankings.
Alcaraz initially faced little resistance from a sluggish Zverev, who had not dropped a set en route to the final. The German struggled with his usually booming serve and made 19 unforced errors in the first set.
What had been billed as a blockbuster turned out to be a one-man show after Alcaraz bagged an early break to take control of the first set.
Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, had saved all six break points he had faced during the group stage, but on Sunday he was struggling to keep pace with Alcaraz from the start.
The Spaniard earned five break points during the German’s first two service games, converting one of them. By the end of the fifth game, Zverev had racked up 15 unforced errors.
While the Spaniard buzzed around the court with his trademark intensity, chasing down every ball and nodding along to the music in the arena during the changeovers, Zverev looked sluggish and slow.
He earned one break back to cut Alcaraz’s lead to 4-2, but three points later his frustration boiled over when he argued with the umpire over a time violation warning.
The second set looked to be following a similar pattern, with Alcaraz keeping the level high and earning another early break.
But Zverev won three games on the trot to lead 5-4 and eventually forced a tiebreak. He could not convert any of his three consecutive set points, however, before Alcaraz clinched the win.
Alongside Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz now forms part of an exclusive list of men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals.

Qatar GP 2026: Dates, schedule, weather, UK start time and how to watch or stream F1 race at Lusail International Circuit live on Sky Sports
Find out the race-week schedule, weather and how to watch the Qatar Grand Prix at the Lusail International Circuit; watch every session live on Sky Sports F1 from Friday, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday
Sunday 22 November 2026 19:38, UK
Formula 1 heads to the Middle East for the last two rounds of the 2026 season with the Qatar Grand Prix hosting the penultimate event this weekend.
After a dramatic Las Vegas Grand Prix which saw 34 lead changes and Max Verstappen pull off a defensive masterclass, the F1 circus has moved to Qatar and the high-speed Lusail International Circuit.
Verstappen, who is set to finish runner-up in the Drivers' Championship behind Kimi Antonelli, won in Qatar last year after McLaren made a poor strategy call when in position for a one-two.
- F1 2026 Calendar | F1 2026 Standings | F1 Gossip Column

Like last year, there is a tyre limit which will create a minimum two-stop race with no driver allowed to do more than 27 laps on a set of tyres in the 50-lap race on Sunday.
This is due to the heavy loads which the tyres are put through in the fast corners which come one after another. The combination of this and this year's 2026 cars could create another fascinating race, particularly with high tension at the front between Mercedes and Red Bull as Verstappen and George Russell's rivalry escalated in Las Vegas.
Qualifying on Saturday is at 6pm UK time with the Qatar Grand Prix on Sunday at 4pm, all live on Sky Sports F1.
Qatar GP track - Lusail International Circuit
The 3.367-mile Lusail International Circuit joined the F1 schedule in 2021 and is one of the highest speed tracks on the calendar due to its fast, flowing corners which punish the tyres but also makes following the car in front difficult.
In the first four editions of the event, which took place when DRS was still in use, most of the overtakes came at Turn One where drivers can make moves on the outside and inside, so it will be interesting to see whether the 2026 regulations create any additional opportunities.
Qatar GP weather
As usual in Qatar, there is no rain forecast across the three days of F1 action with temperatures at around 26C for Qualifying on Saturday and the race on Sunday.

items.title: 'This cannot continue'.- Ferrari to hold fresh Leclerc-Hamilton talks after collision
items.summary:
Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc clashes 'cannot continue' after Las Vegas GP with Frederic Vasseur to speak to drivers again
Ferrari's drivers involved in costly on-track incident for second time in three races, with Leclerc given penalty in Vegas; Frederic Vasseur bemoans a "lack of respect"; watch
items.text:
Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc clashes 'cannot continue' after Las Vegas GP with Frederic Vasseur to speak to drivers again
Ferrari's drivers involved in costly on-track incident for second time in three races, with Leclerc given penalty in Vegas; Frederic Vasseur bemoans a "lack of respect"; watch every session of the Qatar GP live on Sky Sports F1 from Friday, with Sunday's race at 4pm
Sunday 22 November 2026 17:03, UK
Ferrari team boss Frederic Vasseur says he will hold further discussions with drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton after their latest tangle in the Las Vegas Grand Prix, admitting such incidents "cannot continue".
After costly clashes in Monza and Mexico City earlier this season, the Ferrari drivers came together when battling over sixth place with 12 laps to go on the Strip circuit in a race dominated by slip-streaming in which the leading runners were covered by a handful of seconds for most of the race.
Leclerc attempted to overtake Hamilton with a move down the inside of Turn Seven but made contact with the Briton, who was spun around. Stewards found Leclerc at fault and handed him a 10-second penalty, which dropped him to 10th place. Hamilton finished seventh.
In an unusually-strongly worded statement in Ferrari's post-race press release, Vasseur said: "For the second time in three races, something unacceptable has happened between our drivers, and this cannot continue.
"We sent a very clear message to both drivers in Brazil, and today during the race we told them to think about the team when racing each other.
"Of course, in this kind of race you cannot freeze the positions because, with the slipstream, if you slow down, the car behind will overtake you.
"But our drivers should have handled the situation differently, as other team-mates did both in front of and behind them.
"Charles knows he made a mistake and apologised, but that doesn't change the result."
Speaking to the written media after the race, Vasseur had said: "All the other teams, they were able to overtake each other 20 times during the race.
"[Kimi] Antonelli-[George] Russell, [Oscar] Piastri-[Lando] Norris, even Isack [Hadjar] overtook Max [Verstappen].
"Honestly, you can't imagine the frustration for me but, for more importantly, for all the guys at the [team]."
What will happen next?
The situation is increasingly frustrating for Vasseur given it was only three weeks ago that he had to resolve the fallout from a first-lap battle between the drivers that likely cost the team a one-two result in Mexico.
Vasseur brought Hamilton and Leclerc together to speak four days later ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, a meeting he said had "cleared the situation" and acted as "a good reset on the mindset" ahead of that weekend. The Frenchman added that they even "left my room joking together".
Immediately after Sunday's race in Las Vegas, the Ferrari team principal held an initial conversation with Leclerc having asked the Monegasque driver to see him before anything else.
Asked afterwards what they had talked about, Vasseur said: "It was not a discussion, I spoke!
"He apologised, he understands, but the result is there. That you do a mistake, you say 'it's my mistake, I'm sorry' but you did a mistake."
Asked what would happen next, Vasseur said: "I want to digest tonight [after the race] and we'll have to sit down tomorrow with both of them and to take a decision."
He added: "I want, once again, to have a discussion tomorrow. Also Charles will digest the situation and I think it's not the right place to discuss with them two minutes after the race.
"I saw Charles a bit down and I told him what I wanted to say but I'd prefer to discuss with him tomorrow about it."
'It's not a matter of rules' - Vasseur insists 'respect' the key between team-mates
The Las Vegas incident has placed renewed focus on what Vasseur will do to try and bring his drivers definitively into line, with scrutiny growing on whether Ferrari will follow the lead of other teams, such as McLaren and Mercedes, and introduce more formal 'rules of engagement' for what is allowed when in team-mate combat.
Hamilton has called for clearer policies in recent months and said after Sunday's race that "hopefully in the background they eventually figure it out".
Vasseur, however, believes the chaotic nature of Sunday's race shows that clean driving between team-mates is all about respect rather than predefined agreements.
"Honestly, it's not a matter of rules," insisted Vasseur.
"What can you do differently except that you have to respect your team-mate? In this kind of race you have to overtake the car who is in front of you. You can't stay behind, it's completely unmanageable.
"It means you just have to do it with respect when it's your team-mate, to take less risk, perhaps to come side by side and to come back behind. But you can't put it on the paper. I think the race of today [Sunday] nobody would write a scenario like this. Nobody can imagine a race like this. It means they just have to act in a professional way.
"Today it was unprofessional."

items.title: Playoff picture taking shape and Mendoza belongs - NFL Sunday Review
items.summary:
NFL 2026 playoff picture taking shape, Travis Kelce has a big day and Fernando Mendoza proves he belongs - NFL Sunday Review
NFL Sunday Review - we reflect on Week 11 in the NFL as Travis Kelce moved past Rob Gronkowski for touchdowns all-time among tight ends, Las Vegas Raiders' No 1 overall draft
items.text:
NFL 2026 playoff picture taking shape, Travis Kelce has a big day and Fernando Mendoza proves he belongs - NFL Sunday Review
NFL Sunday Review - we reflect on Week 11 in the NFL as Travis Kelce moved past Rob Gronkowski for touchdowns all-time among tight ends, Las Vegas Raiders' No 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza gave evidence he belongs and the Pittsburgh Steelers look in danger in the AFC playoff race
Monday 23 November 2026 07:14, UK
It's an oft trotted out cliché that 'football season starts after Thanksgiving'. Well, with the American holiday only three days away, the NFL playoff picture is truly starting to take shape going into the stretch run.
The San Francisco 49ers (9-1) further asserted their dominance in the NFC with a thumping 35-10 victory over the Minnesota Vikings and their much-vaunted defense in Mexico City - the final International Series game of the season - while the Buffalo Bills (9-1) share the same record as the AFC top seeds, albeit they were far less convincing in their 26-9 dispatching of the one-win Miami Dolphins.
Josh Allen threw two interceptions to allow the Dolphins to hang around until the Bills pulled away late. He and the team will need to sharpen up for their mouthwatering Thanksgiving night meeting with the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) - live on Sky Sports NFL from 1.20am, Friday - that could ultimately end up deciding where the road to the Super Bowl runs through in the AFC.
- Latest NFL fixtures, results and UK kick-off times
- Get latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract
However, it's below the Bills and the Chiefs, and the 49ers on the other side of the conference divide, where things are really starting to get interesting.
The Denver Broncos (8-2) are also in the mix for top billing in the AFC, after claiming a sixth straight against the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) have the opportunity to match that mark with a Monday night victory at the Washington Commanders.
The Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) stumbled at the New York Giants (6-3-1), whose impressive victory strengthened their grip on the NFC East division, which the Dallas Cowboys (5-6) are still in the hunt for after hanging 51 on the Tennessee Titans defense.
The Jaguars' loss was far from fatal, with the Titans, along with the Indianapolis Colts and the Houston Texans all floundering in their division, though the Pittsburgh Steelers' (6-4) shock loss at the Philadelphia Eagles might well have opened the door to the latter in the race for a wildcard berth.
The Texans, who started the season 0-4, now sit 4-6 and - after a meeting with a Baltimore Ravens team in the midst of a six-game losing streak - will likely have the opportunity to match the Steelers' record when the two teams meet in a fortnight, following Pittsburgh's tricky assignment against the Broncos where they'll try to avoid dropping three in a row.
Meanwhile, back in the NFC, the greatest intrigue lies in the NFC North and the four-way battle unfolding for the division, with the Detroit Lions (8-2), Chicago Bears (8-2), Vikings (7-3) - even with their chastening loss to the Niners - and Green Bay Packers (6-4) all currently playoff bound.
Mind you, they all have the looming threat of the wildcard-hunting Los Angeles Rams (6-4) and defending Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks (6-4) from the NFC West.
It makes the Thanksgiving night clash between the Lions and Bears in Detroit - live on Sky Sports NFL from 6pm, Thursday - even more crucial.
See, 'football season (really does) start at Thanksgiving'.
What we learned
The Cowboys' offense is unstoppable!
Quite literally.
Lost in amongst how historically bad their defense is - even the one-win Titans scored on five of their first six possessions, one week on from the 49ers managing to score 46 points and a staggering 584 yards against them - is how impressive their offense is, and needs to be!
The Cowboys are just the fourth team in NFL history to allow at least 20 points in each of their first 11 games and still win at least five of those games. They have allowed 20 points in 18 straight games dating back to Week 12 of last season.
But Dak Prescott threw four touchdown passes and ran in another score as Dallas found the end zone on each of their first six drives in their 51-30 thumping of the Titans to somewhat mask their continued defensive woes.
Fernando Mendoza looks the real deal.
There's still teething issues as the No 1 overall draft picks eases his way into NFL life - most notably the game-sealing pick-six he threw that ensured he starts his career with back-to-back defeats in his first two starts. But there was a lot to like too.
Mendoza and the Raiders hung with the Broncos far longer than many expected, with it being just a one-score game when the rookie QB tossed that costly interception.
Prior to that, he completed 18 of 37 passes for 267 yards and three passing touchdowns - his first in the NFL.
"I felt more comfortable than last week," Mendoza admitted afterwards. "I was able to settle in and able to see the entire field better.
"If you just do your job, your momentum is going to swing your way eventually."
Overreaction or reality?
Are the Steelers in danger of dropping out of the AFC playoff picture?
It certainly looks like they're in trouble. The 19-16 reverse in Philadelphia not only was the Eagles' first win in eight games, it was the Steelers' second straight loss, with Aaron Rodgers, who turns 43 on December 2, looking every bit his age as he limped to 95 passing yards when going 17 of 20 in the first half.
That turned into 227 yards by the end of the game after some garbage-time stat-padding, but it's looking a little rough for the Steelers, who currently occupy the seventh and final playoff berth in the AFC and have a dire run of stellar defenses to come over the next three-week stretch in the Broncos, Texans and Jaguars.

items.title: PS Sing’Oei Defends Kenya-DRC Relations, Warns Against External Interference
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 23 – Foreign Affairs Principal Secretary Korir Sing’Oei has defended Kenya’s relations with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), warning against what he described as attempts by individuals in foreign capitals to create tensions between the two neighbouring countries.
Sing’Oei
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 23 – Foreign Affairs Principal Secretary Korir Sing’Oei has defended Kenya’s relations with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), warning against what he described as attempts by individuals in foreign capitals to create tensions between the two neighbouring countries.
Sing’Oei said Kenya and the DRC shared deep historical, economic and security ties that should not be undermined by external narratives that disregard the realities of communities living across the region.
In a statement posted on X, the Foreign Affairs PS accused unnamed individuals of manufacturing insinuations about relations between Nairobi and Kinshasa, arguing that such efforts ignored the everyday interactions and shared interests of people in the region.
“There are manufacturers of innuendo against Kenya-DRC relations — seated pretty in far away capitals, with little regard for the lived reality of people in the region. They must be stopped,” he said.
He emphasised that the relationship between the two countries was rooted in shared economic and social interests, with communities across the Great Lakes region maintaining close connections through trade, family ties and cross-border movement.
“Kenya and DRC are not abstractions on a map. We share deep connections, trade, security, and brotherhood. Our people cross, trade, marry, and build together daily — from Goma to Bunia to Kinshasa to Nairobi,” he said.
Sing’Oei further criticised individuals he accused of manufacturing tensions for social media attention, financial interests and foreign agendas, arguing that their narratives overlooked the realities of ordinary people living in the region.
“Those who manufacture tension from a distance, for clicks, for funding, for foreign agendas, do not know the market woman in Goma, the truck driver on the Northern Corridor, the mother in Ituri. Washindwe!” he added.
Sing’Oei’s remarks come a day after President William Ruto and his DRC counterpart Félix Tshisekedi agreed to work towards restoring full diplomatic relations between Nairobi and Kinshasa.
The agreement was reached during the high-level Quadripartite Political Summit in Oyo, Republic of the Congo, on Sunday, November 22.
The two leaders committed to restoring diplomatic representation at ambassadorial level, resuming the Joint Grand Commission for Cooperation and strengthening regular diplomatic consultations.
They also agreed to deepen cooperation in trade, economic development, security and culture while working together to advance regional peace and stability. aa.com.tr+2
The diplomatic rapprochement follows a prolonged period of strained relations between the two countries over disagreements linked to the security situation in eastern DRC.
Republic of the Congo President Denis Sassou N’Guesso facilitated the summit, while Togo’s President of the Council of Ministers, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, participated in his capacity as African Union mediator.
Sing’Oei’s statement signals Kenya’s emphasis on rebuilding bilateral trust and protecting the economic, diplomatic and social connections linking the two countries.

items.title: Israeli attacks on medics in occupied West Bank surge by 350%: Rights group
items.summary:
Israeli attacks on medics in occupied West Bank surge by 350%: Rights group
Physicians for Human Rights Israel says medics face ‘dangerous escalation’ in violence from soldiers and settlers.
Palestinian healthcare staff in the occupied West Bank are increasingly coming under attack from Israeli sold
items.text:
Israeli attacks on medics in occupied West Bank surge by 350%: Rights group
Physicians for Human Rights Israel says medics face ‘dangerous escalation’ in violence from soldiers and settlers.
Palestinian healthcare staff in the occupied West Bank are increasingly coming under attack from Israeli soldiers and settlers, according to Physicians for Human Rights Israel (PHRI).
A report released on Monday documented a 350-percent surge in incidents involving Palestinian healthcare workers between 2022 and 2024, noting that emergency responses increasingly face assault, threats and intimidation from Israeli soldiers and settlers – even when clearly identifiable as medical staff.
As part of the report, 25 medics were interviewed, and one paramedic from the Nablus area described how Israeli soldiers prevented him from reaching a wounded man.
“I was standing close to the wounded man. I could have reached him easily, but the soldiers stopped me. He lay there bleeding until he died. Only then did they leave, and we were able to reach him,” he said.
Interviewees described physical assaults, threats at gunpoint, verbal abuse and humiliating searches. All of them said they were on edge, worried that they could be stopped, attacked or prevented from reaching patients.
“Every phone call means taking a risk. And every time I leave home, there’s a chance I won’t come back,” an ambulance driver said.
The PHRI report also documented cases where medics were forced to continue treating patients while facing threats and violence themselves.
The report author, Imran Anati, said there had been a “dangerous escalation” since October 7, 2023, when Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza started.
“These are not isolated incidents, but a systematic assault on Palestinian emergency medical care for which Israel bears responsibility,” he said.
Last year, the World Health Organization recorded 233 attacks on healthcare in the occupied West Bank, including 165 incidents affecting medical transport.
Israeli checkpoints regularly force ambulances to take long detours to reach hospitals, with some patients dying en route and pregnant women forced to give birth outside hospitals.
PHRI has previously warned that the medical system in the occupied West Bank is “collapsing”.

items.title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed
items.summary:
Countries have failed to reach a major new deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey.
Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference
items.text:
Countries have failed to reach a major new deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey.
Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history.
But the final deal proved unacceptable to the EU, Pacific island nations and others because it failed to directly mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.
Meanwhile, many poorer countries objected to the absence of any clear financial commitments from richer nations to help them adapt to the impacts of rising temperatures.
The last time a COP’s main political agreement collapsed like this was in 2009 in Copenhagen.
UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, in his last COP before he steps down, said he was “deeply disappointed”.
He took aim at what he called “powerful fossil fuel interests” who he said were taking “a page from Big Tobacco’s playbook: distorting the science, delaying policy, blocking action, and piling up huge profits while people everywhere pay the price”.
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whose country co-hosted the talks, attributed the failure to “difficult geopolitical times”.
“That is the reality,” he said on Monday.
After two weeks of negotiations, exhausted delegates were presented with a new, draft deal in the early hours of Sunday to try to break the deadlock.
But the words “fossil fuels” did not appear anywhere in the text. The only indirect reference to coal, oil and gas was a nod to a deal agreed at COP28 in 2023, when countries agreed to “transition away” from fossil fuels in energy systems.
The EU’s representative, Irish Minister Darragh O’Brien, made it clear that the EU “strongly” objected, saying that the “decisions go nowhere near the level of ambition needed to tackle climate change”.
“It is unconscionable that we would have a climate pact that makes no mention of fossil fuels,” he said.
Other countries, such as Panama and the Marshall Islands, also criticised the deal for doing nowhere near enough to tackle the pace of climate change.
A first draft of the deal on Monday mentioned “fossil fuel” or “fossil fuels” six times, but that was unacceptable to oil-producing nations.
Saudi Arabia’s delegate Mohammad Ayoub said that Arab countries “continued to engage in good faith” but argued that they only accounted for a small proportion of historical greenhouse gas emissions.
Russia warned not to “turn to slogans” over coal, oil and gas, claiming that if countries moved away from fossil fuels too quickly it would lead to “fuel poverty”.
Climate advocates reacted with dismay at the failure of the talks.
Former US vice-president and climate advocate Al Gore said it was “outrageous that a handful of petro-states have veto power over any mention of fossil fuels”.
The COP process was “in need of significant reform”, Gore wrote on X, as most countries sought “to move forward in good faith.”
“It’s time that we empower those leaders with a reinvigorated multilateral process that reflects the latest science and represents the will of the majority of the world,” he added.
Another major sticking point has been money for poorer countries to adapt to the impacts of climate change, such as more intense heatwaves and more severe droughts.
Last year at COP30 in Brazil, nations agreed to triple the finance for that purpose.
But this year’s deal contained no reference to concrete figures, nor the baseline against which that pledge would be measured. This raised fears it would give richer nations too much wriggle room.
“Rich nations and polluting governments cannot keep arriving empty-handed,” said Mohamed Adow of Power Shift Africa, an African climate and energy think tank.
The UK’s Energy Secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, described the failure to reach a political agreement as “immensely disappointing”.
“This only strengthens our resolve to work with partners around the world on the genuine progress made in Antalya on tackling the climate crisis,” she said, adding that the UK’s commitment was “unwavering”.
While talks were hosted in Antalya in Turkey, Australia led the official negotiations – creating what some observers described as a chaotic dynamic.
Chris Bowen, Australian government minister and COP31 president of negotiations, said there were “unbridgeable red lines” in the discussions.
He pointed to “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”. At the same time, “the impacts of climate change are getting worse”, he said, raising the stakes.
The year 2026 could end as the hottest on record and has brought extreme weather and natural hazards to much of the world, from summer heat and drought in Europe to flash flooding in Nepal.
And COP31 was the first annual UN conference to formally discuss how one of the key international targets for limiting climate change would be missed.
In the Paris talks of 2015, nearly 200 countries agreed to try to limit global warming to 1.5C above pre-industrial levels of the late 1800s, aimed at avoiding some of the worst effects of climate change.
The UN says the Paris deal has driven “near-universal” climate action. In the early 2010s, global warming of 4C or more was thought to be a serious possibility by the end of the century.
Now, the world is likely to limit warming to about 2.8C by 2100 based on current government policies, the UN says.
But action has not been fast enough to meet that Paris goal, with the world likely to “overshoot” 1.5C of long-term warming in the next few years.
Many countries say they are committed to eventually bringing warming back down to 1.5C, but that will require an ambitious ramping up of technologies – which do not yet exist at scale – to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.

items.summary:
Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
- Published
A seven-year-old boy has been rescued from the rubble of a residential building in Dymer, in the Kyiv region, after 14 hours. Overnight Russian strikes on the village killed 11 people, Ukrainian official
items.text:
Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
- Published
A seven-year-old boy has been rescued from the rubble of a residential building in Dymer, in the Kyiv region, after 14 hours. Overnight Russian strikes on the village killed 11 people, Ukrainian officials have said.
The attack occurred in the early hours of Sunday. A 79-year-old woman was also rescued alive from the collapsed building, Kyiv's regional head Tymur Tkachenko said.
A strike on a private home in Bila Tserkva killed one more person and set the building ablaze, he added.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 wounded in a separate strike on Vyshneve, also in the Kyiv region, that hit a grocery store on Sunday.
Ukrainian authorities said the boy in Dymer is in stable condition and was taken to hospital, and have thanked everyone involved in saving his life.
Zelensky and Ukraine's national police also confirmed the rescue of the boy.
In a Telegram post, Tkachenko said the 79-year-old woman rescued from the rubble was receiving treatment in hospital.
Earlier he said six people were injured in the attack, while others were still missing.
Zelensky said more than 130 people are involved in emergency operations at the scene, and that they will continue until they have "complete information about every single person".
Sending his condolences to the families and loved ones of those killed, he said the strike struck the residential building, "practically blowing a section of it to smithereens".
Zelensky added that "rescue efforts are complicated by constant new air raid alerts and renewed threats".
The strike hit the building at 05:00 local time, when families were still asleep, Ukraine's minister of internal affairs Ivan Vyhivskyi said.
More than 70 strikes have been launched across 10 Ukrainian regions as of Sunday evening, Vyhivskyi added.
In his video address posted online, Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 injured in a strike on an "ordinary grocery store" in Vyshneve.
Mayor Illya Dikov wrote on social media that three children were among the injured.
Russia also struck a power substation in the Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukraine's Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky said in a post on X., external

items.title: Omanyo Urges Ruto to Intervene Over Harassment of Kenyan Fishermen by Ugandan Officers
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 23 – Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has appealed to President William Ruto to intervene in the persistent harassment, arrests and alleged extortion of Kenyan fishermen by Ugandan security officers operating on Lake Victoria.
Omanyo urged Ruto
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 23 – Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has appealed to President William Ruto to intervene in the persistent harassment, arrests and alleged extortion of Kenyan fishermen by Ugandan security officers operating on Lake Victoria.
Omanyo urged Ruto to engage his Ugandan counterpart, President Yoweri Museveni, through diplomatic channels to address the recurring disputes threatening the livelihoods of fishing communities along the Kenya-Uganda border.
Speaking in Budalangi, Busia County, during Ruto’s Western Kenya development tour, Omanyo said Kenyan fishermen continued to face intimidation, arbitrary arrests, detention and destruction of their fishing equipment while carrying out their daily activities on the lake.
“I am appealing to you, Mr President, to call President Museveni and address the exploitation of our fishermen on Lake Victoria. Our fishermen are forced to pay as much as Sh30,000 when arrested by Ugandan authorities,” she said.
The ODM Secretary General revealed that more than 50 fishing boats and pieces of equipment belonging to Kenyan fishermen had been destroyed over the past five years, causing significant financial losses to families dependent on fishing.
She also appealed to Ruto to secure the unconditional release of Kenyan fishermen detained in various Ugandan prisons, warning that their continued incarceration had worsened the economic difficulties facing their families.
Omanyo said the recurring incidents required urgent diplomatic intervention, arguing that Kenyan fishermen should not continue losing their livelihoods while accessing resources in a shared water body that supports millions of people across the East African region.
The disputes have remained a longstanding concern among fishing communities in Busia, Siaya, Kisumu, Homa Bay and Migori counties, where fishermen have repeatedly reported arrests over alleged trespassing into Ugandan waters, confiscation of boats and fishing gear, and demands for money before their release.
In August 2025, 24 Kenyan fishermen from Ringiti Island in Homa Bay County were arrested by Ugandan security officers, while six boats were confiscated.
In another incident reported in April 2026, 15 fishermen from Remba Island were released after paying a combined Sh50,000 fine following their arrest over alleged trespass and fishing-related violations.
The incidents have persisted despite diplomatic engagements between Kenya and Uganda aimed at harmonising fishing regulations, streamlining licensing requirements and improving security cooperation on Lake Victoria.
During bilateral discussions in May 2024, the two countries agreed to sensitise fishermen on licensing requirements and acceptable fishing equipment. They also agreed that arrests should be conducted by uniformed security officers to minimise extortion and confrontations.
Beyond diplomatic intervention, Omanyo and other leaders urged the national government, through the State Department for Fisheries, to promote modern fish-cage farming as an alternative source of livelihood for fishing communities.
They argued that investment in aquaculture would boost fish production, create employment opportunities for young people and reduce pressure on the lake’s fish stocks, which have contributed to increased competition among fishermen.
Omanyo called for government support in establishing modern fish-farming facilities and providing fishermen with technology, training and financial assistance to diversify their income sources.
She said diplomatic engagement, improved security surveillance and investment in alternative fishing technologies were necessary to protect Kenyan fishermen, promote peaceful coexistence with their Ugandan counterparts and safeguard communities dependent on Lake Victoria.

NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 23 – Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has pledged to ensure all government project contracts are made public, warning that reluctance by public officials to disclose contractual details should raise concerns about transparency and accountability.
Sifuna said the refusal by the govern
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 23 – Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has pledged to ensure all government project contracts are made public, warning that reluctance by public officials to disclose contractual details should raise concerns about transparency and accountability.
Sifuna said the refusal by the government, to disclose details of contracts was a red flag, arguing that Kenyans have a right to know how public resources are committed and spent.
The Senator vowed to make openness in public procurement and government contracting a priority, promising that all project agreements would be accessible to the public under his leadership.
“When you see Kasongo refusing to disclose details of contracts, it should raise a red flag. I am the one who will ensure all project contracts are open and of public knowledge,” Sifuna stated.
His remarks come amid growing public scrutiny over government spending, procurement processes and the management of public resources, with calls for greater transparency in the award and implementation of public projects.
Sifuna’s pledge signals a push for stronger public oversight of government contracts, particularly those involving significant expenditure of taxpayers’ money.
Making such agreements publicly accessible would enable citizens to scrutinise project costs, contractual obligations, timelines and the entities awarded government tenders.

items.title: UNICEF Urges Kenya to Protect Children’s Funding Amid Declining Foreign Aid
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 23 – The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has urged the national and county governments to safeguard funding for education, healthcare, child protection and social protection programmes amid declining international aid, warning that funding cuts could leave vulnerable chil
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 23 – The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has urged the national and county governments to safeguard funding for education, healthcare, child protection and social protection programmes amid declining international aid, warning that funding cuts could leave vulnerable children exposed to greater risks.
UNICEF Representative to Kenya Dr Shaheen Nilofer made the appeal during World Children’s Day celebrations at the United Nations Office in Nairobi on Friday, calling on governments to prioritise children’s needs in budget allocations.
“Investing in children is no rocket science. You can still be able to redeploy and re-prioritize,” Nilofer said while responding to concerns over declining official development assistance and its potential impact on services targeting children.
She warned that reduced funding could disproportionately affect children living in poverty, those with disabilities and others facing limited access to essential services, increasing their vulnerability to exploitation and hazardous labour.
Nilofer urged governments to protect allocations for education, healthcare, child protection and social assistance programmes, including cash transfers for orphans and vulnerable children.
She said governments must balance infrastructure investments with spending on essential services that directly benefit children, particularly those from disadvantaged households.
The UNICEF representative also called on county assemblies to prioritise children’s welfare when approving budgets, noting that decisions made at both levels of government determine whether essential services reach vulnerable communities.
“We’re reminding that members of the county assembly, when you’re doing a budgeting, please make sure the centrality of the children must be in front of the budget,” she said.
Nilofer cited children in counties such as Mandera and Turkana, where poverty, disability and other forms of disadvantage can overlap, limiting access to education, healthcare and protection services.
She also raised concerns that inadequate social support could push some children into hazardous employment, including unregulated mining activities in parts of Migori and Turkana.
On declining international assistance, Nilofer said UNICEF was working with governments and development partners to identify ways of sustaining essential services.
She called for greater private-sector involvement in programmes benefiting children and urged governments to strengthen domestic resource mobilisation to reduce dependence on foreign assistance.
Despite the funding challenges, Nilofer acknowledged Kenya’s progress in education, healthcare and efforts to address harmful practices affecting children.
She said improvements in school enrolment, maternal and child health, and other social programmes reflected the contributions of government institutions, development partners and civil society organisations.
However, she cautioned that recurring emergencies, including droughts, floods and disease outbreaks, continued to undermine progress and place additional pressure on services targeting vulnerable communities.
The concerns come amid persistent inequalities in children’s access to basic services, particularly in rural areas where poverty and limited access to healthcare, education and adequate housing continue to affect their welfare.
Earlier this month, Kenya became the 80th country to sign the Intergovernmental Declaration on Children, Youth and Climate Action, committing to place children’s rights and needs at the centre of climate policies and investments.
The declaration came amid concerns that approximately 12 million of Kenya’s 24.6 million children face moderate to very high risks from climate change and disasters.
Friday’s World Children’s Day celebrations were held under the theme “My Day, My Rights, My Future,” bringing together children and their caregivers for activities aimed at raising awareness about children’s rights.
The event featured a treasure hunt, games and other interactive activities through which children learned about their rights while engaging with their peers.
Among the participants was 12-year-old Raziel, who identified the treasure hunt as his favourite activity, saying the celebration had helped him better understand children’s rights.
“I learned that children deserve a lot of rights like an adult,” he said.
Raziel also urged people to treat children with kindness, noting that they would play an important role in shaping the future.
Parents attending the celebrations called for greater awareness of children’s rights and the responsibility of families and communities to protect them.
Nyagwaga Luoch Koriom, who attended the event with her two children aged 10 and 13, said the celebrations provided an opportunity for parents and guardians to reflect on how they treat children.
She emphasised the importance of education, provision of basic needs and protection from abuse, urging communities to take action whenever they witness the mistreatment of children.
“For example, right to clothing, right to school, and every other right that we know,” she said.
Koriom also called for greater attention to girls’ education and stronger measures to protect children from sexual abuse and other forms of violence.
World Children’s Day is observed annually on November 20 to commemorate the adoption of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989.
The convention recognises children’s rights to survival, development, protection and participation in decisions affecting their lives.
The celebrations underscored the need to translate commitments to children’s rights into practical action, including sustained funding for essential services and stronger protection mechanisms for vulnerable children.

items.title: Sifuna Takes Linda Mwananchi Movement US Tour to Maryland
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 23 – Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna is set to take his Linda Mwananchi Movement’s United States tour to Maryland on Monday, where he is expected to engage Kenyans in the diaspora, meet elected officials and discuss political developments in East Africa.
The Maryland engagements form
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 23 – Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna is set to take his Linda Mwananchi Movement’s United States tour to Maryland on Monday, where he is expected to engage Kenyans in the diaspora, meet elected officials and discuss political developments in East Africa.
The Maryland engagements form part of an ongoing outreach campaign by Sifuna and his allies to popularise the movement beyond Kenya, with a programme targeting diaspora communities, Generation Z groups and political leaders.
The visit follows earlier engagements in New Jersey and Pennsylvania, where the team officially opened a Linda Mwananchi Movement office in Hackettstown before travelling to Allentown for a church service and a town hall meeting at The Palace Center.
The Maryland leg will feature a business community dinner at Spark Hotel on Monday evening, followed by an East Africa Politics and Policy Meeting in Washington, DC, on Tuesday.
The programme also includes a luncheon with Afri Thrive and Maryland elected officials, as well as a formal dinner on Tuesday evening.
On Wednesday, Sifuna’s delegation is scheduled to hold a brunch with women from the Washington metropolitan area, engage members of the 6.25 Movement and Gen Z Movement, and conclude the day’s activities with a town hall meeting.
The US tour is part of the movement’s broader efforts to establish an international support network and strengthen its organisational presence among Kenyans living abroad.
The outreach comes as political formations begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 General Election, with diaspora communities increasingly featuring in political mobilisation, policy discussions and fundraising initiatives.

items.title: Ruto Mourns Former South African Deputy President Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 23 – President William Ruto has sent a condolence message to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa following the death of former Deputy President Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, describing her as a trailblazing stateswoman and champion of gender equality.
In a condolence letter, Ruto co
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 23 – President William Ruto has sent a condolence message to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa following the death of former Deputy President Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, describing her as a trailblazing stateswoman and champion of gender equality.
In a condolence letter, Ruto conveyed Kenya’s sympathies to the South African government, the bereaved family and the people of South Africa following Mlambo-Ngcuka’s death on Friday.
“On behalf of the Government and the People of the Republic of Kenya and on my own behalf, I convey our heartfelt condolences to Your Excellency, and through you, to the bereaved family and friends, the Government and the great People of the Republic of South Africa,” Ruto wrote.
The President described Mlambo-Ngcuka as a reformist and champion of women’s rights, leadership, equality and peace, highlighting her contribution to South Africa’s political transformation and public service.
He noted that before becoming a Cabinet Minister and eventually Deputy President, she fought against apartheid and played a role in ensuring gender rights were enshrined in South Africa’s post-apartheid Constitution.
Ruto also recognised her contribution to reforms in South Africa’s economic and mining sectors, saying she served her country with diligence and dedication.
Mlambo-Ngcuka also served as Executive Director of UN Women and United Nations Under-Secretary-General, where she championed initiatives aimed at advancing women’s participation in leadership and international peacekeeping.
Ruto said she pushed for the eradication of harmful gender stereotypes and increased women’s participation in United Nations peacekeeping operations.
At the continental level, he credited the former Deputy President with playing an instrumental role in brokering a peace deal in Ethiopia’s Tigray conflict.
“South Africa, Africa and the world have lost a remarkable woman who gave her whole life for gender equality and peace,” Ruto stated.
He further expressed Kenya’s solidarity with the South African government and the Mlambo-Ngcuka family as they mourned her death.
“Kenya stands in solidarity with your Excellency, the Mlambo-Ngcuka family, the people and the Government of the Republic of South Africa as we mourn and honour the life of a pragmatic reformer, a trailblazing stateswoman, peacemaker and gender equality advocate,” he said.
Mlambo-Ngcuka served as South Africa’s Deputy President from 2005 to 2008, becoming the first woman to hold the position. She later led UN Women from 2013 to 2021.

items.title: Kalonzo Demands Aug 11 Deadline for 2027 Presidential Results, Questions IEBC
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 23 – Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka has challenged the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) to commit to declaring presidential election results by the morning of August 11, 2027, while demanding clarity on the future of voter registration ahead of
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 23 – Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka has challenged the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) to commit to declaring presidential election results by the morning of August 11, 2027, while demanding clarity on the future of voter registration ahead of the expiry of its technology contract.
Kalonzo also renewed pressure on IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon to address opposition concerns over the voters’ register, results transmission and electoral technology, warning that the opposition would not endorse an election process it considers unprepared or lacking independence.
Speaking during a church service at AIC Mbaikini in Wamunyu Ward, Mwala Constituency, Machakos County, on Sunday, November 22, Kalonzo defended the opposition’s decision to walk out of a stakeholders’ meeting with the electoral commission on Thursday.
He said the opposition had attended the meeting in good faith but left after finding what he described as an unprepared and insufficiently independent commission.
“We went in good faith on Thursday, and we found no independent, impartial, and prepared commission. We will not lend our names to a bungled election,” Kalonzo said.
His remarks followed Ethekon’s Friday response to the walkout, in which the IEBC chairperson said abandoning the meeting would not resolve the concerns raised by political parties. Ethekon maintained that the opposition had left before the Commission made its presentation and invited stakeholders to submit written proposals.
Kalonzo, however, accused the commission of failing to acknowledge previous submissions from the opposition, insisting that its latest statement did not address their concerns.
“You have our letters. Detailed, written, and submitted, and you never acknowledged them. Your statement did not answer our demands on the voters’ register, results transmission, and technology,” he said.
The Wiper leader insisted that every vote must be counted at the polling station, openly verified and declared as cast, arguing that the process should not take several days before a presidential winner is announced.
He challenged the commission to ensure presidential results are declared by the morning of August 11, 2027, a day after the scheduled August 10 General Election.
“Declare the results by the morning of August 11. It is not rocket science. Brazil counts well over a hundred million votes and knows its winner that night. India counts nearly a billion and finishes in a day. Kenya has about 22 million voters. What is the problem?” he posed.
Kalonzo outlined several demands he wants the IEBC to address before the opposition resumes engagement with the commission.
He called on Ethekon to immediately publish an agenda for future consultations, prioritising an audit of the voters’ register, constituency-level results and electoral technology.
He also demanded an explanation of how voter registration would continue after the expiry of the Smartmatic technology contract on Tuesday, November 24.
“Before the Smartmatic contract expires on Tuesday, tell Kenyans how registration will continue,” he said.
Kalonzo added that the opposition was prepared to return to the negotiating table if the commission addressed the concerns and conducted the discussions publicly.
“Do that, and we will sit with the Commission in public,” he stated.
The Wiper leader further revealed that the opposition had prepared a draft IEBC Amendment Bill aimed at ensuring presidential election results are available by the morning after voting.
The Smartmatic contract’s impending expiry has emerged as a key concern in the wider debate over the commission’s preparedness, particularly amid legal challenges affecting the procurement of replacement election technology. The Standard+1
The opposition leader also criticised President William Ruto’s latest State of the Nation Address, describing it as the President’s fourth and last address before the 2027 General Election.
He accused the Head of State of focusing on infrastructure achievements while failing to address concerns surrounding alleged abductions and enforced disappearances.
“He counted kilometres. Kenya counted the missing. A State of the Nation Address that cannot say the word ‘abduction’ is a progress report for a construction company,” Kalonzo said.
He questioned the government’s response to families whose relatives have allegedly been abducted, arguing that many parents were still seeking answers about the whereabouts of their children.
“When the history of these four years is written, it will not be written from that speech. It will be written from the files in the mortuary and from the parents who had to bury and report missing their children,” he added.
Kalonzo also appealed to the African Inland Church (AIC) leadership to reject donations and Harambee contributions he suggested were drawn from public funds.
He cited the Catholic and Anglican Church of Kenya (ACK), urging AIC to adopt a similar position on contributions from public officials.
“Ask the question: this is your salary. How can you donate Sh5 million at one event? Rudishia hiyo pesa,” he told the congregation.
The church service was attended by Democratic Party leader Justin Muturi, Machakos Woman Representative Joyce Kamene, Deputy Governor Francis Mwangangi and Senator Agnes Kavindu.
Others present included Makueni Senator Dan Maanzo, Kitui Central MP Makali Mulu, Embakasi South MP Julius Mawathe, Wiper Chairman Jamleck Kamau and party spokesperson Ndegwa Njiru.
The remarks come as political parties intensify their engagements with the IEBC over electoral reforms, voter registration and preparations for the August 2027 General Election.
