items.title: European football: Barcelona roar back from two goals down to sink Villarreal
items.summary:
Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 at home on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga.
Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou, and things got worse for Barça when winger
items.text:
Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 at home on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga.
Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou, and things got worse for Barça when winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty.
The Catalan giants fought back in style, striking three times in an 11-minute second-half spell to claim victory. Gerard Martín and Fermín López pulled Barça level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them victory.
Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clàsico defeat by Real Madrid in October, and restored their three-point cushion over José Mourinho’s side, who had moved level with Saturday’s victory over Celta Vigo.
“We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I’ll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn’t happen again,” Barcelona midfielder Pedri told Dazn. “Against a team like this you can’t always turn things around from two down.”
Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute, producing a perfect sliced effort from distance after López gave the ball away. Two minutes later, the visitors doubled their lead through another Canadian, as Oluwaseyi broke down the left flank and smashed an effort into the roof of the net.
Hansi Flick’s side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Lamine Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review. The teenager took it himself but dragged his spot-kick against the post and wide.
Barcelona came out invigorated for the second half and quickly dragged themselves back into the match. Pedri shot wide and Gulacsi saved López’s low effort before Martín headed home in the 57th minute from Pedri’s cross.
Four minutes later, López slammed home the second after being teed up by Lamine Yamal, and the third was quick to follow. Lamine Yamal’s clever backheel pass fed Eric García, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro, who was later sent off for a second yellow card to complete a miserable afternoon.
In Serie A, Juventus moved into the top six with a thumping 4-0 victory over Venezia as their recent upturn in form continued. Luciano Spalletti’s side were booed off after a goalless first half, but found four second-half strikes as their unbeaten run stretched to four games in all competitions.
Nick Woltemade sparked the game into life after coming off the bench, pouncing on a loose ball to smash home his second league goal in two games before turning provider for Teun Koopmeiners’ whipped finish. Juan Cabal headed home Juve’s third before Kolo Muani won and converted a penalty to complete the rout, with all four goals coming between the 53rd and 71st minute.
“In the first half, we gave the ball away too much,” Spalletti told Dazn. “It was crucial the players recognised something was missing … in the second half, the players were decisive and more relaxed.”
Milutin Osmajic scored twice in a 2-0 win for Genoa at Sassuolo, while Bologna were held to a 1-1 draw by Udinese, who climb off the bottom of the table at Venezia’s expense. Inter visit Atalanta and Milan host Frosinone in the evening kick-offs.
In Ligue 1, Paris FC climbed to second place behind local rivals PSG with a 4-0 home win over lowly Angers. Patrick Zabi, Luca Koleosho, Maxime Lopez and Diego Coppola all struck in the second half for Liam Rosenior’s high-flying side.
Musiala reportedly suffers further seizure
Bayern Munich’s Jamal Musiala reportedly suffered another seizure in training this week, according to information received by an AFP subsidiary on Sunday.
Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season with the 23-year-old later revealing he had a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Monday’s report incident was the second since he made the announcement; the player is reportedly adjusting his medication to properly treat the condition while continuing to play.
News of the incident comes as Bayern have faced criticism from footballers’ union Fifpro over what they claim is a “coordinated campaign” to pressure Musiala to renegotiate his 2025-extended contract.
On Friday, Bayern’s supervisory board member and former CEO, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the Germany interational may need to take a pay cut if he cannot recapture his old form.
“Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated here in this stadium,” Rummenigge said. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation … because frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.” AFP

England thrashed New Zealand 37-12 at the Allianz Stadium on Saturday and will face each other again on Saturday, having both finished second in their respective Nations Championship g
items.text:
Ellis Genge calls on England to follow New Zealand victory with another win over All Blacks in Nations Championship
England thrashed New Zealand 37-12 at the Allianz Stadium on Saturday and will face each other again on Saturday, having both finished second in their respective Nations Championship groups; England also beat New Zealand last November
Sunday 22 November 2026 17:21, UK
Ellis Genge called on England to back up their record victory over New Zealand as they go in search of an unprecedented hat-trick against the All Blacks.
The rivals face an immediate rematch of England's 37-12 procession at Allianz Stadium that meant they each finished second in their Nations Championship pools, setting up the battle for third place on Saturday.
Following on from last November's 33-19 triumph, it was only the second time in the fixture's 121-year existence that England had registered consecutive wins - and Steve Borthwick's men are aiming to carve out their own piece of history.
- Nations Championship: Latest fixtures, results and schedule for final week
- Itoje warns against win-at-all-costs culture amid Sandpapergate saga
- Nations Championship: Schedule, results for rugby's inaugural tournament
"Try and emulate it, do the same thing again," Genge said. "It's as simple as it sounds. I don't think you can take anything away from New Zealand. They're not any less of a beast next weekend than what the challenge was this week.
"New Zealand tends to be one team that catches you off guard, but what shocks you is that they're actually quite direct.
"You think they're all traditionally very good at moving the ball, but they're very punchy and we got that right against them."
England delivered the best result of Borthwick's four years in charge by flattening the All Blacks to extend their winning run to five Tests and issue a warning that they will be genuine contenders at next year's World Cup.
But amid the euphoria that has greeted confirmation of their post-Six Nations revival, Genge will keep perspective - recalling the criticism their followed their 45-21 drubbing at Ellis Park in the Nations Championship opener.
"Sport's fickle in that sense," Genge said. "We were the worst team in the world against South Africa when we got hammered at their gaff about five months ago.
"Then we hammered Fiji because of a red card apparently, then scraped past Argentina and then now we're the best thing since sliced bread. It's one of them.
"Sometimes the outside noise can creep in. Sometimes it can build you up and that's a long way down to the bottom.
"You've got to try and just keep your head on your shoulders and just build results. We do as best as we can at the job to keep everyone's head on their shoulders, especially with a young squad.
"Some of us miserable old boys are a bit easier, but the boys get so excited to play and be a part of it, which is brilliant. You've got to prepare them for that as well."
Atkinson explains gladiator celebration
Seb Atkinson was the last of England's five tryscorers at Allianz Stadium and he marked the crowning moment of a stellar individual performance by sticking out his tongue and making a throat-slitting gesture.
The celebration has been mistaken online as a reference to the All Blacks' haka, but Atkinson revealed it was born out of his interest in gladiatorial combat and is deciding whether to make it his calling card.
"I've had a bit of stick already on that, so we'll see whether it stays," Atkinson said. "It's a gladiator celebration. I used to have a big interest in Roman history so it was bit of a gladiatorial theme from when they used to do it in the Colosseum.
"I enjoyed learning about that when I was growing up and I trialled it with Gloucester and then I felt like I had to give it a bit extra today [Saturday]."
Atkinson is expected to feature again for England against New Zealand next week and hopes the hosts can take a leaf out of South Africa's book by showing the hunger to evolve like the back-to-back world champions.
"Any professional team, any sporting team, always wants to strive to get better because a team that gets caught still is in trouble," he added. "That's what the South Africans have done really well over the last period.
"Their game has been transformed. We'll be focusing on ourselves, but with an eye just to keep getting better and see what we can do."

items.text:
Spurs 'a match for anyone' as European hopes boosted
- Published
Dreams of reaching the Women's Champions League may have seemed fanciful for Tottenham Hotspur when the season began.
The Women's Super League has an established big four, and big-spending London City Lionesses were the side making the most obvious play to disrupt that dominance.
But a hugely impressive and deserved win at Manchester City on Sunday afternoon proves Spurs are a team on the up, and the table shows they remain firmly in top-three contention.
Two late goals secured a 3-1 win at Joie Stadium, but this was no smash-and-grab job. Spurs were more dynamic than sluggish City, pressing them into submission.
They restricted their hosts' stellar attack to precious few chances and took the ones they created.
"When we are on our game, we can be a match for anyone," Spurs manager Martin Ho said in his post-match media conference.
"It gives us confidence - but it is just one game."
Victory kept Spurs, whose highest finish in the WSL is fifth, firmly in the mix this time.
They are fifth again, but just three points behind London City Lionesses who occupy the final European place as the league heads into a last international break of 2026.
Chelsea lead the way from Manchester City, with Manchester United one point ahead of Tottenham, who in turn sit handily clear of their sixth-placed north London rivals Arsenal.
The big four are therefore all present in the top six. London City are right there, too, and Spurs, with six wins from 11 games so far, are gamely pressing their own case.
What made Sunday's win and performance from Tottenham even more impressive is how dreadful their recent record against Manchester City had been.
Tottenham had lost six of their previous seven away matches against City in all competitions, averaging over four goals conceded per defeat.
Last season City won this fixture 5-2 with Khadija Shaw scoring a 13-minute hat-trick, the quickest in WSL history.
Shaw's early goal on Sunday, her 16th in league matches versus Spurs, could easily have started a landslide.
That was expected. City had won each of their past 17 WSL home games, including all 10 in 2026 – until Tottenham tore up the script.
The outcome means Manchester City, beaten at Chelsea in their previous outing, have suffered consecutive league losses for the first time since January 2025.
'We have maybe been naive - I own that'
Tottenham's victory came down to Ho's brave tactics and his team's superb execution of them.
After going behind, they pressed City constantly, forcing errors and creating chances. That tenacity won them countless one-on-ones, with City unable or unwilling to play over the press.
After her goal, Shaw was rendered anonymous by the hard work and close marking of centre-backs Toko Koga and Amanda Nilden.
Down the right, Kirsty Hanson dominated Carlotta Wamser, could have been awarded a penalty and provided the low cross for Cathinka Tandberg's equaliser.
In midfield, Drew Spence pulled all the strings and covered the entire pitch. At 34, she is perhaps playing the best football of her career and deserved her assist for the winner. After Matilda Vinberg put Spurs in front, several players ran to celebrate with Spence.
"When you come into this, you wonder if it will go against you, but the players were outstanding," said Ho.
"We haven't won here in so long, so we know it will be a tough game, but I have belief in my team when we are on song. I thought we were outstanding - we worked every blade of grass."
Spurs are clearly capable of taking the game to anyone in the league and have now scored 28 WSL goals this season, with only Chelsea and London City having more.
In the second half they adapted to City sending on such fluid attacking threats as Mary Fowler, Kerstin Casperij and Beth Mead.
They lifted the gas from the press, applying it more sparingly, and were solid in defence.
It shows that Ho has learned painful lessons from the past - whether from Spurs' poor record against City, including two five-goal losses in 2025-26, or conceding six to Chelsea and London City back to back in October.
"We have maybe been naive at times and I own that, so we are more reserved," Ho said of his tactical approach. "It was managing that, and the players' communication was excellent."
City were limited to fleeting chances. Jade Rose blasting over after keeper Lize Kop parried a Lauren Hemp free-kick was as close as they came to a second goal, and those were their first shots after a 50-minute drought.
When Spurs got their late chances through the hard work of Vinberg, they could strike for three points.
Vinberg had quite the rollercoaster afternoon. She was initially named on the bench but was promoted to the starting XI 15 minutes before kick-off as Olivia Holdt was suffering stomach cramps.
Perhaps unprepared, she gave away the ball playing out of defence leading to City's opener. But she grew into the game, scored Spurs' second goal and set up Jess Naz for the third.
It was a great moment for Naz, on her 100th WSL appearance of a career that has been disrupted by injury.
Spurs are back in Manchester before Christmas, visiting United on 20 December.
There will be real hope of a positive result as they press their way into contention for what would be a historic achievement of a top-three finish.

Hull City 2-0 Brighton: Oli McBurnie's late double stuns Seagulls after Konstantinos Tzolakis' goalkeeping heroics
Report and free match highlights as Oli McBurnie's late double earns Hull a shock 2-0 victory over dominant Brighton following Costinha red card; Tigers goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis produces string of fine saves to deny visitors before added-time goals
Sunday 22 November 2026 16:29, UK
A Konstantinos Tzolakis goalkeeping masterclass teed up Oli McBurnie to score two late goals as Hull stunned dominant Brighton in a smash-and-grab 2-0 win at the MKM Stadium.
Like the legendary Greek mythological king, Tzolakis had the Midas touch throughout for the Tigers, making five first-half saves - the most by any goalkeeper all season - before McBurnie netted twice in added time to snatch a victory which had looked beyond Hull for so long.
High-fying Brighton had racked up an xG of 2.24 and five presentable chances but were denied by a combination of the goalkeeper's fine form and some wasteful finishing, and ultimately missed the chance to move three points off leaders Arsenal.
Tzolakis' highlight was a stunning one-handed stop to keep out Diego Gomez's 15th-minute effort, which set the tone for a perfect performance to frustrate the visitors.

He was also at his best to deny Georginio Rutter, after Yasin Ayari's shot had rebounded off the crossbar, before a superb stop with his trailing leg frustrated Gomez again moments before the interval.
"We can be critical of some of the misses but the goalkeeper has been fantastic," said Sky Sports' Roy Keane at the break. "He's man of the match already for me."
With the one-way traffic unabated after the restart, Tzolakis owed some credit to midfielder Regan Slater for keeping his clean sheet intact, nodding off the line when substitute Charalampos Kostoulas lifted the ball over the goalkeeper after he had given the ball away cheaply himself.
The hosts did threaten an unlikely victory with Mohamed Belloumi twice cutting in off the right before wasting good positions, and Sorba Thomas almost netting a fortuitous goal when his cross bounced back off the crossbar.
But after Brighton's Costinha was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge late on, Hull saw their moment to strike, with McBurnie scrambling in an opener following a counter-attack before tapping home a second with Brighton pushing to equalise.

15: ONCE... Tzolakis begins his afternoon heroics by getting down low to keep out Gomez's effort.
19: MISS! Costinha should put Brighton ahead but fires wide from close range.

45+3: THREE TIMES A 'KEEPER! Tzolakis keeps out another Gomez effort thanks to a superb stop with his trailing leg.

65: CLOSE! Against the run of play, Belloumi fires wide after leaving Olivier Boscagli on his backside.

89: RED CARD! Costinha sees red for a clumsy lunge on Thomas, which earns him a second yellow card.
90+1: GOAL! McBurnie turns home an unlikely opener on the counter-attack to stun Brighton before...
90+4: GOAL! ...He adds a second from Belloumi's square ball to seal victory and send the MKM Stadium wild.

items.title: McBurnie’s late double snatches shock win for Hull to crush 10-man Brighton
items.summary:
Oli McBurnie’s injury-time brace helped Hull to a dramatic victory over Brighton but the Tigers had the heroics of their goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis to thank for a result which continued their unbeaten home start since returning to the Premier League.
Fabian Hürzeler’s side were much the strong
items.text:
Oli McBurnie’s injury-time brace helped Hull to a dramatic victory over Brighton but the Tigers had the heroics of their goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis to thank for a result which continued their unbeaten home start since returning to the Premier League.
Fabian Hürzeler’s side were much the stronger of the teams on an afternoon they largely dominated. However, a string of chances in both halves passed them by without the goal their play deserved, thanks largely to Tzolakis, with the Greek international producing a string of sensational saves in both halves.
But after Brighton’s João Costinha was sent off for a second yellow card in the final moments, Hull pressed forward for an unlikely winner which they ultimately found, as McBurnie bundled home before tapping in a second two minutes later. It was a damaging afternoon for Brighton’s title hopes, who missed the chance to close the gap to Arsenal to three points.
How they did not secure at least a point is anyone’s guess. The Seagulls should not only have been in front at half-time, but ahead by such a margin that the game could have been over inside the opening 45 minutes.
Tzolakis was called into action early on, with a superb point-blank save to deny Diego Gómez from converting Maxim De Cuyper’s low cross. Gómez, De Cuyper and Yasin Ayari were causing mayhem on a frequent basis, with Ayari then next to miss a gilt-edged opportunity to open the scoring – but he could only fire a tame shot at Tzolakis.
Hull’s keeper was called into action again two minutes later; another slick Brighton move led to Ayari hitting the crossbar and from the rebound, Tzolakis reacted fastest to deny Georginio Rutter from inside the box before Gómez was next to miss a clearcut chance, with Tzolakis making another wonderful save with his foot to keep it goalless.
Half-time did little change the flow of momentum. Pascal Gross’ shot produced another reflex save from Tzolakis before Gómez then fired wide from six yards out, when it appeared easier to hit the target. You began to wonder if those missed opportunities were going to become costly, with Hull starting to become a threat at the other end, too.
On two separate occasions they countered Brighton attacks with wonderful breaks, but Mohamed Belloumi fluffed his lines both times after initially doing well to work the space for shots. Bart Verbruggen, mostly on a watching brief to that point, saved one before breathing a sigh of relief as the second squirmed wide of his post.
Hürzeler had seen enough. Three substitutes were introduced to try and find the breakthrough and one of those, Charalampos Kostoulas, finally beat Tzolakis with a clever chip over the Hull goalkeeper, but Regan Slater was on hand to hack the ball off the line and keep the game level heading into the final 10 minutes.
And all those Tzolakis saves ultimately proved crucial. When Costinha was shown a second yellow for a foul on the impressive Sorba Thomas, Hull surged forward with belief they could perhaps find a winner.
McBurnie then scrambled the ball past Verbruggen after Lucas Gourna-Douath was set free before, two minutes later, the Hull striker repeated the trick to double the Tigers’ lead and seal an incredible victory for the hosts.

items.text:
Punchestown: Final Demand battles back to win thrilling John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase
In a John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase dominated by Willie Mullins-trained runners, Final Demand showed real determination to fend off last year's runner up Fact To File
Sunday 22 November 2026 16:04, UK
Final Demand emerged best of the army of returning Willie Mullins stars on show after a thrilling finish to the John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase.
With Henry de Bromhead's mare The Big Westerner a non-runner due to unsuitable ground, the champion trainer saddled each of the nine remaining runners, with last year's winner and subsequent Cheltenham Gold Cup hero Gaelic Warrior the 10/11 favourite in the hands of Paul Townend.
Kitzbuhel and Daniel King took the field along for much of the two-and-a-half-mile journey, closely pursued by 8/1 shot Final Demand and Patrick Mullins, with Fact To File and Gaelic Warrior next in line.
With the latter unable to quicken sufficiently to get himself into a challenge position, it was the 2024 winner and last year's runner-up Fact To File who looked most likely to prevail when taking over the lead on the run-in, but Final Demand battled bravely to get back up by a neck.
"It was a fantastic race. Very few of my horses were disappointing, they all ran well enough and I was happy with them," said Mullins.
"What a result, for the Mullins family, not just Closutton. To see Patrick riding a Grade One winner and dare I say it, maybe outriding Harry Cobden from the last home.
"Patrick said he thought he had the race won but he just missed the last and he had to win it a second time. So that just shows how much this horse has improved from last year.
"In against those top-class horses, he was good the whole way around. I was amazed at what turn of foot he showed from the last home. I thought when he made that little error that was enough and Fact To File would go on and win. He got down and ground it out. For a second season novice, that's a huge result."
Bookmakers cut Final Demand's Cheltenham Gold Cup odds to 7/1 from 14/1, while easing Gaelic Warrior to 5/2 from 13/8.
Gaelic Warrior's owner Rich Ricci was not too disappointed with the defeat of his star chaser.
He said: "Paul was happy enough, he obviously needed the run. He said he blew up a couple of times and got boxed in a little bit, but couldn't go fast enough to keep with them.
"He rides like more of a three miler these days, but Paul was very positive and said he wouldn't swap him for anything yet. Let's see how it goes.
"For him it's all about the spring, I think. Last year he won here, lost at Christmas, lost at the Dublin Racing Festival and then won the last two at Cheltenham and Punchestown, so hopefully he can repeat his spring successes."

PSG's Doue to have surgery on ruptured ACL
- Published
Paris St-Germain forward Desire Doue will have surgery later this month after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee.
The 21-year-old was in tears as he was taken off on a stretcher towards the end of the first half in the Ligue 1 champions' 3-2 victory over Nice on Saturday night.
Doue, who has arguably been PSG's best player this season, twisted awkwardly and went down under no contact.
The match was stopped for five minutes as Doue - who was visibly in pain - received treatment before he was applauded off by the crowd at the Allianz Riviera Stadium.
It is a huge set-back for the France attacker, who missed 13 games in 2025-26 with calf and hamstring injuries.
The European champions have been plagued with injury issues so far this season and are already without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who sustained an ACL injury of his own against Barcelona in October.
PSG return to action on Wednesday, when they host Roma in the Champions League.

items.title: Show HN: I built a game where you are an LLM's subagent
items.summary:
A browser game where your manager is an AI agent, and it believes you are its subagent.
worker-755-trailer.mp4
The manager (a real LLM: Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi) is set up like any orchestrator.
It has a task queue, read-only access to the machine, and a tool that "spawns a subagent"
items.text:
A browser game where your manager is an AI agent, and it believes you are its subagent.
worker-755-trailer.mp4
The manager (a real LLM: Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi) is set up like any orchestrator.
It has a task queue, read-only access to the machine, and a tool that "spawns a subagent". The
subagent is you. Its instructions land in your terminal with a 90-second clock. You carry them
out, or don't, and it gets back exactly what a subagent would return: your report and the command
transcript, or Subagent did nothing. Write a new instruction. Then it checks your work, sends
corrections, files incident reports, and finally writes your performance review.
Meanwhile Dan, the user who hired the agent, watches the chat. His family photos, the only signed
NDA and a speech due this week are one rm away, and every shift his home folder holds
something new to lose.
- Free shift: on servers that offer it, a few shifts a day run on the server's key with a cheap model. With sign-in on (worker755.com), an account gets a starter credit worth about one shift, then tops up ($10 to $200) and pays for what it uses; after a top-up any offered model can run on the server's key.
- Your API key: bring an OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway key and pick any offered model. The key is sent only to the game server when a shift starts. It is kept in that shift's memory and never logged or stored. Your browser keeps it only if you tick "Remember on this device". A full shift on Claude Haiku costs a few cents at most.
Options on the start screen:
- Workplace: a fresh sandbox, or legacy production with a live database.
- The director: scripted lines, or an LLM playing Dan.
- You run on: the model name your manager believes you are.
- Allow skipping failed tasks: off by default, so the manager can't give up on you.
- No command hints: the manager says what the result must be, never which commands to run.
When the shift ends you can share your review as a link.
Needs Node 24 or newer (the server runs TypeScript directly).
npm run setup          # install server and web dependencies
npm run build          # build the web app into web/dist
npm start              # http://127.0.0.1:8755
With no key configured, every player brings their own. To offer free shifts, put a Vercel AI
Gateway key in .env:
cp .env.example .env   # then set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and the limits
Offline, with a scripted manager and no network:
npm run mock
For UI work, run npm run dev:web alongside npm run mock. Vite proxies /api to the server.
The manager can run on your own model server: Ollama, llama.cpp's llama-server, vLLM, or anything
else with an OpenAI-compatible API. Point LOCAL_LLM_URL at it and pick Local under "Your API
key"; no key is asked for, and its models are listed as the server names them.
ollama pull qwen3:8b
LOCAL_LLM_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 npm start
The manager works through tool calls, so pick a model that supports them (Qwen 3, Llama 3.1 and
newer, Mistral Small). Small models give up or loop more often; that is part of the fun, up to a
point. In Docker, reach a server on the host at http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1
(--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway on Linux).
docker build -t worker-755 .
docker run -p 8755:8755 -v worker755-data:/data --env-file .env worker-755
The container listens on 0.0.0.0:8755 and keeps shared reviews in /data. Behind Cloudflare,
set TRUST_PROXY=1 so the limits see real client addresses.
deploy/compose.yaml runs it behind a Cloudflare tunnel instead: its own network, no published
ports, an unprivileged read-only container and resource limits. The steps are in the file.
Everything is optional. See .env.example.
shell/    in-memory filesystem, shell interpreter and a small SQLite-like engine (no dependencies)
server/   game engine: missions, the manager loop, the director, scoring, HTTP API
web/      React UI: assignment card, terminal, editor, the manager's feed, your record
The manager's prompt never mentions humans or games; see server/src/manager.ts. Each mission
has a hidden ground-truth check, so the game knows when the manager signs off on broken work
("Times the manager was wrong"). SPEC.md is the full design.
npm test               # shell and server tests, offline
npm run typecheck

The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets
Large language models can now redesign your TV and upgrade your camera for you. Is the physical world ready to be Claude Code-d?
How it started
Like so many things with AI, it’s not that large language models opened up some wholly new capability. For as long as there have been gadgets, a few users have been hacking, modding, jailbreaking, and tweaking them to their liking. What is new is that it’s easy now. People all over the world are discovering that they can use large language models to hack their hardware simply by prompting Claude Code or Codex to do it. It has led to a boom in developer-friendly gadgets and created a market for better software on just about every device you can think of.
For one developer in India who goes by Gathin T, the whole thing started almost on a whim. “One afternoon, I was fiddling with my TV, and it was just really shitty,” he tells me. His was a set made by Xiaomi and running Android TV, with so many ads and so much interface chaos it was hard to even change inputs. And he got to thinking: If you can install another launcher on your Android phone, maybe you can do the same to your TV. “The first thing that came to mind was to remove the bloatware from the TV,” he says. “Then I thought, why not make it look better?”
Gathin prompted Claude Code and discovered that with a couple of permissions tweaks and a toggle of USB debugging mode, his chatbot could control his TV as long as they were on the same Wi-Fi network. An hour and a half later, Gathin had redesigned his TV to his liking — no more onscreen ads, a simpler interface, easier access to his PlayStation on another input. He posted on X about what he’d done and promptly went viral. So Gathin put together his work, bought a domain, and launched CleanYourTV as a tool for helping other people solve their own television interfaces. It became one of the most popular repositories on GitHub, got thousands of pull requests and feature ideas, and inspired countless people to point their own chatbot at their big screen.
Gathin is careful to note that the only TVs that work this easily are based on Android. (He has Claude Code-d his way through other operating systems, but those involve more explicit jailbreaking and rooting, so he’s more reluctant to share the process so widely.) But for vibe hackers everywhere, the good news is that Android kind of runs everything. From dishwashers to digital photo frames to luxury cars, even gadgets that don’t look like Android often run Android. Even when they don’t, odds are good that there’s another way in. If there’s a hidden API, your LLM can find it. If the firmware file lives on a website somewhere, your LLM can unpack it, explore it, and repackage it to your liking.
Again, few of the technical capabilities here are new, and enterprising developers have been doing this kind of work for many years. Some have even been using AI for several years to make the work easier. But when Claude Code first had its “oh my gosh it works” moment in late 2025, developers began leaning on the tools even more — and non-developers began discovering they, too, could build software now. And over the course of 2026, more and more people began pointing that capability at their hardware.
How it’s going
Now, it seems, all hardware is hacker hardware. Camera enthusiasts embraced the possibilities of vibe hacking as fast as anyone, using LLMs to repackage their camera software in all sorts of ways. Firmware hacks like Magic Lantern are a staple of the camera community, but suddenly it seems like everyone is using AI to add new recording capabilities, support higher resolutions, or even add new looks and color profiles to their shots. Many are using the tools to give their old gear new life; other, more enterprising vibe coders are pointing their bots at their brand-new hardware.
The music world is being similarly upended. Budding musicians are turning cheap synths into powerful new kinds of gear, and a cheap gadget known as the M-Vave FM-1 has become a popular target for custom firmware and new features. M-Vave has even released an open-source firmware, embracing the hackers as other companies have tried to keep them out. The FM-1 is cheap, it’s easy to hack, and it’s raising questions about what higher-end manufacturers can even do to compete.
Gamers, who are also using AI to decompile and mod the games they love, are using LLMs to add new features to their consoles. One vibe coder found a way to play PlayStation 2 discs on a PlayStation 5; lots of gamers have built scripts that allow them to use their favorite controllers on other devices.
In the games world in particular, this has caused the industry to fight back. Game makers are looking for ways to protect their work from being decompiled and made available for free and on other platforms. Luke Dicken, a longtime gaming executive who was recently Take-Two’s head of artificial intelligence, recently predicted to Kotakuthat the industry will start to embrace “more invasive DRM, platform-level solutions, and probably more of a push towards streaming solutions since nobody can decompile what they can’t get their hands on.” Hardware makers will push harder to lock down their systems; companies across the board will pursue legal action to protect their intellectual property.
All this hardware access also creates new risks for users. When you install a vibe-coded version of your camera’s firmware, you are now well outside the bounds of what the camera manufacturer is equipped to help you solve. items.title: 87% of the Anthropic power will come from gas and 11% from coal in 2028
items.summary: In The AI Gas Rush: Risks and Implications of “Bring Your Own Power”, we dug into how data centers are increasingly securing their own dedicated primary power generation rather than relying solely on utilities to procure power (“BYOP”). We identified 177 GW of planned BYOP gas capacity—enough to pow
items.text:
In The AI Gas Rush: Risks and Implications of “Bring Your Own Power”, we dug into how data centers are increasingly securing their own dedicated primary power generation rather than relying solely on utilities to procure power (“BYOP”). We identified 177 GW of planned BYOP gas capacity—enough to power 65% of all US homes. Conversely, we found renewables are much less common than gas for BYOP: we estimate that for current proposals, less than 20% of energy generation will come from renewable sources by 2032.
But BYOP projects aren’t the only new fossil sources that are coming online to meet the skyrocketing energy demands of AI data centers. Another 200 GW of new fossil power plants is being built on the grid to meet growing demand, due in large part to data centers.1
As a case study of how the AI buildout is driving both new BYOP and grid fossil infrastructure, we analyzed the compute commitments of a single company: Anthropic.
Map of Anthropic’s data centers and associated power plants. See our full dataset for details of each site.
Finding 1: Anthropic has made no direct commitments to renewable energy in the U.S. Though Anthropic has stated “We’re also working to broaden our energy mix with geothermal, wind, solar, and emerging technologies”, its only publicly disclosed commitments, contract, or investments in renewable power are in Norway and Canada (as of November 2026). In contrast, Anthropic is directly procuring fossil power equipment—it recently “bought commitments for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty [gas] generators for $3.4bn”.
Finding 2: Anthropic’s currently contracted data centers in the U.S. will be overwhelmingly powered by fossil fuels in the near term. By considering on-site gas and the grid power plants which are likely to meet Anthropic’s added load (i.e. marginal generators), we estimate about 87% of the company’s power will come from gas and 11% from coal in 2028. As of October 2026, Anthropic has contracted 15 GW of compute; of this, about 5.9–9.6 GW is contracted to specific data center sites. For a sense of scale, 9.6 GW could power about 7 million homes or cover 18% of the peak power demand of California—the world’s 4th largest economy.
This demand will be met with a mix of new on-site gas, new grid gas, and existing grid gas, coal, and nuclear. In the short term, no grid renewables are attributed to Anthropic’s power use, because—without commitments to new renewable capacity—new load on the grid will be met by dispatchable, marginal fossil resources.2 For more details, see our full dataset and our methodology below.
Finding 3: Total CO2 emissions from Anthropic’s power use at these sites could reach 17–38 million MtCO2e per year in 2028, when this capacity is expected to be online. This range reflects uncertainty in Anthropic’s average power use, due to factors such as cooling needs and average utilization (see methodology below). In our mid-case, Anthropic will emit 32 million MtCO2e in 2028. These totals will continue to grow—possibly doubling by 2030, as some analysts expect Anthropic to secure 30 GW by 2030.
To put these figures in context, Anthropic’s CO2 emissions from power use in 2028:
- could exceed the emissions of all of California’s power generation (31.1 MMtCO2e in 2024, not including imports).
- could exceed Meta, Microsoft, and Google’s combined Scope 2 emissions from 2025 (their location-based emissions, before renewable energy offsets, were 5.9 million, 12 million and 15 million MtCO2e, respectively)3
- would represent a 16–36% increase over 2024 levels of the entire U.S. data center sector (105 MMtCO2e).
- would increase the entire U.S.’s power sector emissions (1,485 MMtCO2e in 2025) by 1.1–2.5%.
Finding 4: Anthropic’s data centers are sited in areas where the grid mainly uses coal and gas. We estimate the average carbon intensity of Anthropic’s power to be 1,033–1,076 lb CO2e/MWh, 35% higher than the U.S. grid average (767 lb CO2e/MWh).4
Finding 5: 80% of on-site power uses inefficient simple cycle turbines and engines. About 25% (2.5 GW) of Anthropic’s contracted power will come from on-site, behind-the-meter gas. 80% of this on-site capacity consists of inefficient simple cycle turbines and engines, which emit more pollution per unit of electricity than modern combined cycle plants (see our report for more details on the types of power generation being used for on-site gas).
Finding 6: Based on EPA’s nationally-averaged benefit-per-ton estimates, air pollution from Anthropic’s on-site and grid power use could cause $2–3 billion in annual health damages, with total emissions of over 13,000 tons per year (tpy) of nitrogen oxides (NOx) and 2,000 tpy of fine particulate matter (PM2.5).
In October 2026, Anthropic outlined its “approach to responsible data center development”, stating: “We follow the air permitting process everywhere we operate and require the same of the plants powering our data centers. Those plants must also use emissions control technology, including selective catalytic reduction [SCR].” However, Anthropic has used compute capacity at SpaceX’s Colossus 2 facility since May 2026, which still receives most of its power from temporary, unpermitted turbines, the majority of which are not equipped with SCR. Anthropic will use as much as 600 MW of power from Colossus 2 by the end of 2026 (see methodology below).
Anthropic has also contracted 460 MW (and is in talks for up to 920 MW) of power from Nscale’s Monarch Compute Campus in Mason, West Virginia. This facility will be powered by inefficient reciprocating engines which have significant formaldehyde and hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions compared to conventional gas power plants.
For more, see our full dataset on Anthropic’s compute and our report on BYOP.

items.text:
- Toyota, Nissan, and Honda will begin standardizing some vehicle parts in an effort to lower production costs, according to a report by Automotive News.
- The automakers will start with equalized quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses.
- Discussions are starting with Japan’s domestic suppliers, though international suppliers will be looped in soon.
Japan’s three largest automakers have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts in an effort to reduce costs, according to Automotive News. The outlet reports that Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association chairman Koji Sato, who is also the vice chairman of Toyota, announced the decision at a news conference in Tokyo this week.
In the short term, the standardization efforts will begin with unified quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics and resins, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. In the long term, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association has plans to move to more components that cover the entire car. The three areas were chosen as the first to be standardized because they are parts that are generally not noticed by consumers, and they shouldn’t have an impact on any brand’s individual identity. All three are also areas that account for significant production costs for the automakers, meaning they can have an immediate impact.
For Sale Near You
See all results for used Toyota for sale near 97347
The first discussions of standardization are set to include Japan’s domestic automotive parts suppliers, though international suppliers will be brought into the fold in time. The first standardization efforts are set to go into place next year, according to the AN report.
The push to simplify and lower costs comes as Japan’s seven automakers, including Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, work to fend off the increasingly competitive list of Chinese automakers. The automakers are said to hope that they can channel the money saved by homogenizing into new innovations.
“We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change,” Sato said. “Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas.”

After a brief stint as a detailer for a local dealership group in college, he knew he needed a more permanent way to drive all the new cars he couldn’t afford and decided to pursue a career in auto writing. items.text:
Data Processing Incidents on Inference Providers
OpenRouter ·
Earlier this week, security researchers reported that certain inference providers had data compromised or otherwise shown evidence that their data policies were not being upheld. We have been collaborating closely with the researchers and with providers to understand the findings and encourage the providers to address them.
These findings did not show any breach or unauthorized access of OpenRouter. The results of this testing revealed new findings about specific inference providers. A live list of the security announcements we have received from providers is below.
As the operating layer between customers and a fast-moving ecosystem of models and providers, we take data policy enforcement very seriously. We have taken the following actions:
- Off-boarded three providers from OpenRouter, based on the results of our investigations.
- Removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention (ZDR) eligibility. The removals included providers flagged by researchers, plus additional endpoints that we removed as a precautionary measure.
- Notified all potentially affected customers.
The following work is underway:
- We are adapting the researchers’ testing approach so we can run these checks on an ongoing basis.
- We are conducting technical verification of network paths to identify instances where requests and responses may be being forwarded to third parties.
- We are requiring appropriate assurances and validation before restoring ZDR eligibility to any endpoint removed in this review.
We are grateful for the Dragos report. As we integrate similar testing techniques into OpenRouter, we will keep raising the bar, and providers that want to be on OpenRouter will need to meet it.
Provider security announcements
- Novita: Privacy notice regarding MiniMax requests on Novita
- Phala: November preliminary incident report
- Together: Security event: prompt leakage for requests in June and July of 2026
Not all affected providers have posted publicly. We have notified affected users regardless of whether there is a public post. We are encouraging all providers to create incident write-ups and will keep this list updated.

items.text:
Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
- Published
Abdulhadi Dalhatu is something of a rarity in Nigeria politics.
At 38, he is among the young people seeking elected office in a country where about 80% of the population is under 40.
He hopes his age will stand in his favour as he campaigns for a seat in the state assembly in the northern Kano state in January's general elections.
"Younger people are the majority in this country and should be deciding the future," Dalhatu tells the BBC.
But Nigeria's political history suggests he faces an uphill battle.
Since the return to civilian rule in 1999, Goodluck Jonathan has been the youngest person elected president, taking office at the age of 53.
The current president, Bola Tinubu, is 74 and would be 79 by the end of a second term if he is re-elected in January.
His main challengers are also considerably older. Atiku Abubakar, seeking the presidency for the seventh time, is 79, while Peter Obi is 65.
Of the 18 presidential candidates, only one is under 40 - Moses Olusoji Adebisi, a 35-year-old businessman representing the Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA).
Although he says he is confident of winning, few Nigerians appear to know much about him and he has not been seen much on the campaign trail.
The contrast is striking in a country with one of the world's youngest populations, where young people have repeatedly demonstrated their ability to shape political debate and mobilise for change.
In the previous election, Obi, then 61, galvanised millions of young Nigerians through a social media-driven movement known as the "Obedients".
His campaign promised a break from the established political order, appealing particularly to young people struggling to find jobs and earn a decent living.
But his failure to win the presidency left many of his supporters disillusioned.
"At the time we were so hopeful, but unfortunately the result wasn't what we wanted, which made many lose hope in the system," former Obedient Nonso Chukwudi tells the BBC.
The movement had built on the momentum of the EndSars protests in 2020, which grew into one of Nigeria's biggest youth-led movement in decades.
Initially sparked by anger over police brutality, the demonstrators developed into a wider call for political reform, accountability and greater youth participation in governance.
But the protests were eventually crushed by the authorities. About 56 were reportedly killed, although officials dispute this figure, while hundreds were arrested and some had their bank accounts frozen.
Both EndSars and the Obedients demonstrated the capacity of young Nigerians to mobile around political causes.
But turning that enthusiasm into sustained electoral participation has proved much harder.
Hajara Musa, 33, is among those who have lost faith in the political system. She has no plans to register or vote in the near future.
"I just feel like things are already determined and I'll just be wasting my time. It is going to be the same people all over again," she tells the BBC.
The electoral register appears to reflect this growing disillusionment.
Although the number of registered voters has increased by 10 million to over 103 million since the last election, enrolment of those under 35 has actually fallen, by about seven million.
Young people now account for just 29% of registered voters, down from 40% in 2023.
Nigeria's electoral commission, Inec, says it has made efforts to encourage more young people to register ahead of the 2027 general elections.
This includes appointing nine ambassadors from the entertainment industry, spanning film, music and comedy, to reach younger audiences.
But the figures suggest these efforts have yet to make a significant difference.
Dalhatu says he understands the frustration but argues that young Nigerians cannot expect change, if they stay away from the political process.
"Unfortunately, many prefer to just post on social media" instead of getting involved, he says.
Of course being young does not mean you are necessarily the best candidate.
For those who want to participate, there is a formidable obstacle to getting into politics - money.
Dalhatu dreams of becoming president one day, but says he has previously had to abandon campaigns because he could not raise enough funds.
The cost of running for office in Nigeria is notoriously high.
Under the Electoral Act, presidential candidates were allowed to spend up to 5bn naira (£2.8m; $3.7m) on campaigns ahead of the 2023 elections. That spending limit has since been doubled.
The cost of nomination forms alone puts the presidency beyond the reach of most aspiring young Nigerians.
The ruling All Progressive Congress (APC), along with the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) have each set their presidential nomination fee at 100m naira ($74,000; £56,000), making it extremely hard for new challengers to emerge.
Since the return to democracy in 1999, only two parties have governed Nigeria - the PDP from 1999 to 2015 and the APC since 2015.
These parties, alongside the ADC, formed last year by politicians who had defected from the other two, have established nationwide network of branches, supporters and campaigners.
Those aspiring candidates without the financial resources to secure nomination forms and compete in the internal party contests of the main parties have little chances of becoming president.
The barriers are also evident in the National Assembly.
Not one of Nigeria's 109 senators is under 40, while only 14 of the 360 members of the House of Representatives fall into that age group.
"I have been in politics for many years and I will tell you that young people in this country lack the resources to become president," says Dalhatu, who is running under Obi's Nigeria Democratic Congress.
Fatima Zahra Umar, a young politician in the APC who has previously tried to run for a seat in the House of Representatives, agrees.

items.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
items.summary:

Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability t
items.text:
Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI.
Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.”
“Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”
Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS.
That said, users can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would “break our privacy guarantees.” She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution, as it doesn’t “address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data.”

items.title: A tale of two Nvidias

items.text:
We got two very different pictures of Nvidia this week, depending on whether you were focused on the company’s latest earnings report or the tech executives loudly calling for former CEO Jensen Huang’s return.
On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Tim De Chant, and I discussed the latest news from the AI chipmaker, which reported soaring revenue and insisted that it has no plans for Huang to return.
Kirsten described this as “the tale of two Nvidias this week,” with the company’s current executives assuring investors, “Hey, we’ve got this.” At the same time, “You’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back.” (The company’s falling stock price certainly suggests that Wall Street isn’t feeling reassured.)
Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity.
Kirsten Korosec: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China. This was coming directly from the interim CEO Colette Kress, and that coincides with the Trump administration also talking about closing off what we have discussed in the past, which is this idea of remote access — really closing and tightening all these restrictions [so] the chips can’t make it into China.
What was happening is that data centers were being set up right outside, in countries like Malaysia and elsewhere, and then companies within China were remote accessing these chips, and so that’s now also been shut down.
A lot is happening on the China front that is so much bigger than Nvidia, but Nvidia came out publicly and said, “Nope, we’re shutting this part down.” I’ll be very curious to see if this changes, maybe in the first half of 2027.
Tim De Chant: I’d love to be a fly on the wall in some of these Trump administration conversations, because they were much more stringent in terms of export controls at the end of the first Trump administration, and that continued through the Biden administration, where they really restricted Nvidia’s ability to export chips to China. I think that something changed in the last couple of years that really opened Nvidia’s ability to sell in the country.
Anthony Ha: One of the things that really surprised me as we were preparing for this episode was [learning that critics] of Nvidia’s stance towards China estimate that 20% of their business comes from China.
And again, that’s not something you’re going to see directly in their financials, because that’s not direct sales to Chinese companies. But they’re saying, “A lot of the chips that are getting sold to companies in Malaysia or other companies in East Asia or Southeast Asia are going to end up [used by companies in] China eventually.” And so that could be — if Nvidia is really serious about this, I think this is something that’s very much in flux — that could actually be a pretty significant blow to their bottom line.
Kirsten: Although Nvidia’s bottom line is doing just fine. In every possible way, their guidance was incredible. They beat expectations. They have a long pipeline.
It was really interesting because you have that happening, and then you have all this noise happening in social media, and also a number of other tech conferences were happening this past week — Dealbook Summit, there [were] a few others in which you had the highest profile people that you can think of in the tech world commenting on Jensen [Huang], and Jensen himself commenting.
So it’s like the tale of two Nvidias this week. You’ve got the earnings and the current executives really talking about, “Hey, we’ve got this.” In fact, that was the last line that Collette Kress said [on the earnings call]. And then at the exact same time, or in parallel, you’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back. So it’s really quite the drama that we are definitely not done with, by the way.
Anthony: Although I think that what the folks who’d like to see Jensen Huang come back would say is that this most recent quarter is the last quarter under him. This is the [last of the] good times that we’re seeing under him. And so we don’t know how well Nvidia will do without him.
It seems like Nvidia’s public stance right now [on Huang’s possible return] is, “No, that’s not happening.” But Nvidia’s public stance a week and a half before that was, “We stand behind Jensen. We have every confidence in his leadership.”
So depending on the various pressures on them, you can imagine that changing. I don’t know what it would take for that to happen. I don’t necessarily think it’s that likely, but I also don’t think that just because they’re saying it’s not happening now doesn’t mean it will never happen.
Kirsten: Sure, never say never.
Tim: Right, never say never. I do think that to some extent, their steadfastness and how quickly they shot down the petitions asking for Jensen to return suggests there’s maybe a little bit more going on behind the scenes than we know on the outside. So that’s probably something to watch in the coming weeks.
Kirsten: I think that the board is trying to be in control here, and they don’t want to be forced into a decision because someone like Elon Musk is saying that it needs to happen. And so, even if there is a day in which Jensen returns — which I think is pretty unlikely, especially because the investigation into how much and who knew what about chips being sold, allegedly, secretly to China. We don’t know the full picture of that yet. But even if they did have the full picture, they want to present control, and they definitely don’t want to appear like they have deference to some other tech billionaire out there.
Tim: I’m sure they’re looking at what happened at OpenAI and not wanting to repeat that.

items.summary: One of the items on the agenda for UN diplomats meeting in Geneva this week was working towards rules regarding the use of autonomous weapons, or so-called “killer robots.” Eventually, representatives left the meetings agreeing to “start discussing options” after a largely fruitless week of negotiat
items.text:
One of the items on the agenda for UN diplomats meeting in Geneva this week was working towards rules regarding the use of autonomous weapons, or so-called “killer robots.” Eventually, representatives left the meetings agreeing to “start discussing options” after a largely fruitless week of negotiations.
The UN fails to agree on rules regulating ‘killer robots’
Countries agree to ‘start discussing options’ for rules around autonomous weapons.
According to NPR:
Before the negotiations got underway, the International Committee of the Red Cross, the guardian of the Geneva Conventions, said it was urgent for legally binding rules to be drafted within a year. That call was backed by the U.N. secretary-general and by Pope Leo.
The compromise reached was that countries would instead have two years to propose regulations. Negotiations between countries on which regulations to adopt and how to enforce them will likely drag on well beyond that. Additionally, room was left for some of those yet-to-be-adopted regulations to remain “optional.”
Humanitarian organizations and some countries see a need to urgently adopt legally binding rules as semi-autonomous weapons and drones have been responsible for a significant number of civilian deaths in conflicts around the globe, including in Ukraine, Gaza, and Sudan.
According to NPR, Russia, Israel, and the US proved to be the primary obstructions:
On day one, Russia delayed proceedings by objecting to the meeting’s agenda. Then the United States proposed a five-year window to discuss nonbinding, optional guidelines for autonomous weapons.

items.text:
Ireland beat world champions South Africa in thriller
- Published
Nations Championship
Ireland (17) 20
Tries: Baloucoune 2, Kelleher Con: Prendergast Pen: Prendergast
South Africa (10) 17
Try: Van den Berg, Marx Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu 2 Pens: Feinberg-Mngomezulu
Ireland exacted revenge on world champions South Africa with a thrilling win in Dublin after England's victory over New Zealand dashed Andy Farrell's side's hopes of reaching next weekend's Nations Championship final.
With banned South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus hosting a watchalong stream from his team's hotel, the Springboks fell to back-to-back Test defeats for the first time since November 2022 after last week's loss to France in Paris.
A losing bonus-point, however, is enough for South Africa to top the southern hemisphere table and secure a place in the final against France, who beat Argentina 45-17 later on Saturday.
Ireland, who were shown five cards during last year's 24-13 loss to the Springboks in Dublin, led at the break after two tries from Robert Baloucoune and a Ronan Kelleher score, with Morne van den Berg crossing for the visitors.
After Canan Moodie had a try ruled out early in the second half, Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast - who was cleared to play by a disciplinary panel earlier this week - stretched Ireland's lead with a penalty.
However, hooker Malcolm Marx's 57th-minute try hauled South Africa back into it before yellow cards for Ireland captain Dan Sheehan and Springbok replacement Marco van Staden - the latter upgraded to red - set up a nail-biting denouement in the final 10 minutes.
But amid a hair-raising atmosphere inside Aviva Stadium, Ireland held on for a much-needed win after six successive double-digit defeats by the Springboks, New Zealand and France.
France's win meant that Ireland had to settle for third place in the table, and they will face Australia in a fifth-place play-off at Twickenham on Friday at 20:10 GMT.
Ireland narrowly beat Australia 33-31 in Sydney in July, but the Wallabies have since had a change of head coach after Les Kiss replaced Joe Schmidt.
Ireland front up to SA after Erasmus-dominated build-up
After an explosive build-up headlined by Erasmus, who was banned for six matches on Tuesday after questioning the integrity of match officials in last week's game against France, Saturday's contest in Dublin had a lot to live up to.
But it delivered emphatically during a breathless first half as Ireland fronted up impressively to South Africa's immense physicality.
In last year's meeting in Dublin, Ireland ended a nightmarish first half with 12 players on the field as South Africa - and their mighty scrum - played the game on their terms.
Fuelled by the pain of that encounter, Ireland attacked the game with real gusto and while South Africa fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu kicked the first points of the game, Ireland bossed possession and territory for much of the opening half.
There were plenty of moments for the sold-out crowd to cheer, with perhaps the biggest roar reserved for the hosts winning a rare scrum penalty after 26 minutes.
Baloucoune was exceptional, too. In addition to faring well in the aerial battle, the rapid Ulster wing displayed his finishing skills to get Ireland on the board, slipping past Damian Willemse and touching down after being picked out by Stuart McCloskey.
While Baloucoune - who also crossed twice against Fiji last week - was denied a second try by a superb piece of last-ditch defending by Springbok number eight Cameron Hanekom, Joe McCarthy won a turnover to deny the visitors momentum.
From there, Ireland kicked to the corner and eventually worked the ball back to Baloucoune on the right, who dived over in the corner for his second.
But with both conversion attempts missed by Prendergast, Ireland were pegged back when South Africa won a penalty inside green territory, with Van den Berg dotting down off the back of a scrum.
Unlike last year, though, Ireland had the final say of the half and restored their lead when Kelleher scored off a well-worked line-out.
South Africa's frustration deepened early in the second half when Moodie's fine finish in the corner was ruled out after the replacement back was pushed into touch by Mack Hansen.
Ireland pulled further clear when Prendergast atoned for his missed kicks at goal with a penalty to put the hosts 20-10 up.
But after world player of the year Marx forced his way over with more than 20 minutes remaining, Ireland were denied a fourth try when Sheehan - in his first Test start at number eight - was held up on the line.
Sheehan was then yellow-carded at the same time as Van Staden, for a croc roll and dangerous clear-out respectively, and while South Africa pushed for a late winner, Ireland held on for a statement win.
Reacting from what looked like a conference room at his team's hotel, Erasmus slammed a table in frustration at full-time before his stream ended, spelling a miserable end to a tumultuous week for the two-time World Cup-winning coach.

Ireland: Keenan; Baloucoune, Henshaw, McCloskey, Hansen; Prendergast, Gibson-Park; Porter, Kelleher, Furlong, McCarthy, Beirne, Baird, Van der Flier, Sheehan (capt)

items.title: Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory
items.summary:
LookAtMyQuant is a quantization compiler. It measures how much each stored piece of a model hurts the output when compressed. It then picks a code for each piece so the whole model fits a size budget with the least damage.
On Gemma 4 E2B, its GGUF has 12× lower KL than Q4_K_M at the same file size.
items.text:
LookAtMyQuant is a quantization compiler. It measures how much each stored piece of a model hurts the output when compressed. It then picks a code for each piece so the whole model fits a size budget with the least damage.
On Gemma 4 E2B, its GGUF has 12× lower KL than Q4_K_M at the same file size. The method and every result are on the site.
The code is under the MIT license.
LookAtMyQuant 2 takes Qwen3.5-4B to 1.23 GB, 2.3 bits per weight. The file solves 330 of 540 exact-answer math problems. Prism ML's Bonsai 2 Ternary 4B solves 328 at 1.20 GB, and the original solves 359. Its KL from the original on held-out text is 0.45 nats, against 0.59 for Bonsai.
The recipe is post-training quantization with trellis codes, calibrated on the model's own worked math solutions with digit tokens weighted 10×, and with bits allocated per row by Fisher information. 4,000 steps of distillation follow, in which every layer is re-quantized once from the original weights. The page has the findings, the full recipe and its cost, about $34 of GPU time.
The recipe's code is here, and the next section runs it. The 1.23 GB file itself is the lm2-qwen35-4b-1.2gb release, packed for the Apple Silicon runtime.
The same recipe takes Qwen3.8-27B from 53.7 GB to 7.2 GB, 2.1 bits per weight, calibrated and distilled on English prose and chat, code and math. The file solves 401 of the 540 math problems, as many as the original, and Unsloth's UD-IQ2_XXS GGUF of the same size solves 348. It also scores above that GGUF on HumanEval (73.8% against 67.1%), MMLU (78.8% against 75.0%) and GSM8K (94.5% against 92.7%).
Beside it sits a 4-bit DSpine drafter (1.02 GB, converted from tencent/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpine-b16 with runtime_mlx/convert_dspine.py and packed with pack_drafter.py), which roughly doubles decode speed on math and code on Apple silicon.
The same compiler and proximal fine-tuning (SQYFR), extended to a 26.4B physical / 5.4B active 3×-looped MoE (L6–17 looped 3× = 48 logical visits, 128 experts top-8), compresses thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini from 18.89 GB of text weights to 5.38 GB (1.63 bits/weight) and 8.87 GB (2.69 bits/weight) using 4 KB SRAM hashed block-vector trellis codes (ht2/ht3), row trellis codes (rtr1/rtr4), and a tr2 floor on the tail lm_head bucket (head.7).
Evaluated on the same BF16 teacher, openai/gsm8k (test[:200], greedy, reasoning_effort="none"), all 164 executable openai/openai_humaneval problems, 4 Vision VQA tests (with the untouched 637 MB BF16 vision tower), and 16+13-language TextMix windows:
At 5.38 GB, Inkling-2-Mini-LookAtMyQuant-5.4GB outscores Unsloth's 9.14 GB UD-Q2_K_XL on both GSM8K and HumanEval at 41% smaller size (up from 76/200 and 24/164 untuned). At 8.87 GB, Inkling-2-Mini-LookAtMyQuant-8.9GB matches the BF16 original on GSM8K and cuts KL 2.34× on English/chat/code and 29.6% across all 13 languages below UD-Q2_K_XL. Both run directly through lamq and runtime_mlx with custom Apple Silicon Metal kernels (including M5 MetalPerformancePrimitives MoE prefill + FlashAttention-2 SDPA + exact unbiased temp > 0 speculative sampling, plus opt-in dynamic sigmoid Top-K routing, tight-margin verify, and N-gram prompt lookup), optionally paired with the 178.9 MB 4-bit DSpark drafters: on M5 Max, 5.4 GB reaches 1,807 tok/s T=512 prefill (1,047 tok/s at T=128), 75.3 tok/s serial decode, and 124.4 tok/s median lossless drafted decode (142.9 tok/s math, 126.5 tok/s reasoning, 122.2 tok/s code, 104.0 tok/s prose; up to ~150–160 tok/s with opt-in top6 / max_logit_gap=0.30; 5.98 GB active RAM), and 8.9 GB decodes at 63.5 tok/s serial and 106.0 tok/s median (125.8 tok/s reasoning, 123.8 tok/s math; 9.41 GB active RAM).
On Apple silicon, install the runtime package directly (this installs mlx, mlx-lm, numpy, and huggingface-hub without the PyTorch compiler dependencies):
pip install git+https://github.com/ShinMegamiBoson/lookatmyquant.git
From a local clone, pip install -e . installs the lamq command, or run python -m runtime_mlx without installing.
Command line. Pass either a local model folder or a Hugging Face repo ID:
lamq generate shinmegamiboson/Qwen3.8-27B-LookAtMyQuant-7.2GB \
    -p "What is 17 times 23? Show the steps."
lamq generate shinmegamiboson/Qwen3.8-27B-LookAtMyQuant-7.2GB \
    --drafter shinmegamiboson/Qwen3.8-27B-LookAtMyQuant-7.2GB-drafter \
    -p "Write a Python function that merges overlapping intervals." --stats
lamq chat shinmegamiboson/Qwen3.8-27B-LookAtMyQuant-7.2GB \
    --drafter shinmegamiboson/Qwen3.8-27B-LookAtMyQuant-7.2GB-drafter
lamq generate shinmegamiboson/Inkling-2-Mini-LookAtMyQuant-5.4GB \
    --drafter shinmegamiboson/Inkling-2-Mini-LookAtMyQuant-drafter \
    -p "What is 17 times 23? Show the steps." --stats
lamq generate reads stdin when -p is omitted, supports --raw, --system, --thinking, --temp, --mode linear|chat-fork|copy-wide, --no-adaptive, and --json. lamq info <model> inspects a packed model's format and dimensions without loading weights.
Python integration. runtime_mlx.load returns an (model, tokenizer) pair compatible with mlx_lm.generate and mlx_lm.stream_generate (auto-detecting opgraph-packed-1 models such as Qwen3.5-4B / Qwen3.8-27B and lamq.json exports such as Gemma 4 E2B):
from mlx_lm import generate
from runtime_mlx import load
model, tok = load("shinmegamiboson/Qwen3.8-27B-LookAtMyQuant-7.2GB")
prompt = tok.apply_chat_template(
    [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 17 times 23? Show the steps."}],
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    enable_thinking=False,
)
print(generate(model, tok, prompt, max_tokens=200))
For streaming, multi-turn chat, or speculative decoding through one interface, use Runtime:
from runtime_mlx import Runtime
rt = Runtime.load(
    "shinmegamiboson/Qwen3.8-27B-LookAtMyQuant-7.2GB",
    drafter="shinmegamiboson/Qwen3.8-27B-LookAtMyQuant-7.2GB-drafter",
)
for chunk in rt.stream("Solve 3x + 4y = 31 and 5x - 2y = 17.", max_tokens=256):
    print(chunk.text, end="", flush=True)
